summary_intro:
Housing Graduate Trainee Programme
This is a graduate programme with real responsibility from day one. Over two years, you'll rotate across several teams at the heart of Clarion's housing operations, building hands-on experience, professional skills, and a genuine understanding of what it means to support residents and communities.
You'll be funded to complete the Chartered Institute of Housing Level 4 qualification, gain exposure to senior leaders, and be supported to apply for permanent roles at Clarion on completion. This is a programme designed to develop future housing professionals and future leaders.
Clarion is the UK's largest housing association, with over 125,000 homes across the country. We exist to solve a problem that genuinely matters, and if you want to spend two years learning everything about housing management whilst making a real difference to residents' lives every day, this is the programme for you.
You'll choose from rotations across the following teams, spending time in several areas over the course of the programme:
The starting point for your journey. You'll work alongside our frontline teams, managing resident enquiries, conducting estate inspections, supporting safeguarding processes, and getting a thorough grounding in day-to-day housing management.
A team that handles complex anti-social behaviour, tenancy fraud, and domestic abuse cases. You'll manage your own caseload, meet service targets, and begin developing people management skills.
Responsible for letting our empty properties as quickly as possible. You'll work with local authority partners, carry out tenancy checks, and gain valuable stakeholder management experience.
A performance and insight-focused team. You'll work with data to improve service delivery and produce a service improvement plan for a real team or local area.
A centralised team managing over 20 housing processes, from mutual exchanges to legal action. You'll see how consistent, high-quality service is delivered at scale across the organisation.
Supporting the transformation of communities through new build, estate renewal, and sustainability projects. You'll liaise with residents going through regeneration and work with development teams on delivery planning.
A dedicated team managing relationships with residents experiencing damp and mould in their homes. You'll be a key point of contact, ensuring timely updates and a positive customer experience throughout.
In each placement you'll lead a project, whether that's improving a local area, reviewing a policy, or auditing a resource. At the end of every rotation, you'll present your progress to your team and members of the management group.
You'll also attend graduate training modules throughout the two years and gain exposure to property management and repairs services, an essential part of understanding our full customer offer.
The tailored programme offers personal & professional skills development through our Graduate Development Programme. You'll have the opportunity to regularly network and learn with other Clarion graduates to develop & apply relevant skills across a range of topics such as change management, strategic thinking, leadership & management.
To complement the practical experience you will gain, we will also pay for you to complete the Chartered Institute of Housing Level 4 qualification.
Upon successfully demonstrating a fully competent performance you will have the opportunity to apply for roles in Clarion Housing. We will provide support to help you grow and develop throughout your time at Clarion.
In exchange for your commitment and dedication, we will provide you with a generous benefits package that includes:
Clarion Housing Group is the UK's largest housing association with homes in over 170 local authorities and a heritage stretching back more than a century. Through our development arm Latimer, we build new homes, while our charitable foundation Clarion Futures runs one of the country's biggest social investment programmes, helping people and communities thrive. As a business for social purpose, we reinvest every penny of surplus into our mission to provide homes for those who need them most, building a better future today.
We are recruiting for these opportunities in partnership with Acrobat Talent.

We are looking for Graduates for our Building Specialists teams, who have an adaptable approach and an appetite to learn in a leading Engineering and Professional Advisory services consultancy. We want you to enjoy working in a collaborative environment where you can apply your skills working for a diverse range of clients and projects.
We are recruiting for Graduates in the following services and locations:
Fire Engineering : London & Guildford
Working as a Graduate in one of our Building Specialists teams, will mean working on exciting and innovative projects. We are proud of the value we can add to any project through the application of our specialist knowledge to solve client problems. We pride ourselves on bringing the latest techniques to the table to ensure that clients get best in class service in what is an increasingly complex design and compliance environment.
You will be embedded in multidisciplinary teams and mentored by experienced professionals, gaining exposure to real-word challenges and innovative solutions. You will be part of a supportive team culture where you’ll receive mentoring and guidance as you develop your skills.
Our teams work on some prestigious assignments, and you will be helping deliver projects such as:
Monklands Replacement Hospital, Scotland
Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle
Control Posts, Heathrow Airport
Our Fire Engineering team is involved in the development of the overall fire strategy for a building, which involves the design of fire protection systems within buildings including means of escape, building layout, smoke control, sprinkler systems, reaction to fire of construction materials,
Working as a Graduate in our Fire Engineering team, you will be helping to protect buildings and occupants from the effects of fire and smoke by ensuring buildings are designed in line with Part B of the Building Regulations (fire safety). This is achieved by following relevant code guidance to produce fire strategy documents and other technical reports to demonstrate a building’s compliance or coming up with specific fire engineered solutions where following code-guidance may not be feasible.
Day-to-day activities could include:
Producing fire strategy reports for proposed and existing buildings.
Writing technical design notes.
Marking up architectural drawings to produce fire strategy plans that outline aspects of the fire strategy.
Reviewing existing documentation relating to the above.
Design team meetings – with disciplines both internally and externally, as well as site visits.
Responding to fire-related queries from other disciples such as IT & Security, facades, MEP, structures, architects etc
Our two-year Graduate Development programme is designed to support personal and professional development and growth through an engaging blended learning experience. The programmes include core business and professional skills training, career development workshops and resources, valuable networking opportunities, mentoring for professional registration and a breadth of on-the-job experience.
Our teams are dedicated to supporting your career growth from the very beginning. Many employees have started as graduates and successfully advanced within the company. We encourage you to achieve chartered status with professional bodies such as ICE, IStructhE, IMechE, and IET, ensuring your development is a priority. You will be fully supported through enrolment in a professional institution’s training agreement, guiding you towards chartered or incorporated status.
You’ll have graduated with at least a 2:2 in a Master’s degree in Fire, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical or Civil Engineering or Physics.

Each investment platform has dedicated teams with deep asset-class expertise, organized globally and committed to maximizing client benefit from their specialist areas. We are an international business: Our 1,160 employees work from 13 locations across Europe, the Americas, and Asia.
Are you curious, driven, and ready to shape your future in Investment Management? At Aegon AM, our NextGen Traineeship is your opportunity to build a strong foundation and grow into a well-rounded asset management professional.
Through hands-on experience, on our two-year fixed-term contract you will gain exposure to different areas of the business and close collaboration with industry experts, you’ll develop the skills, insight, and confidence to thrive in a fast-moving environment. summary_intro:
£28,000 - £40,000 (dependent on skills and experience)
25 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, company pension and other benefits
Align Property Services is creating a brand-new Graduate AI & Automation Analyst role to help shape how artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are used across our business.
We’re looking for someone who is genuinely enthusiastic about AI, with a natural curiosity for how emerging technologies can be applied in practical ways to improve how people and organisations work.
This is a unique opportunity to join an award-winning, multidisciplinary property consultancy and play an active part in improving efficiency, productivity, and digital capability across our teams. With clients at the core of our approach, you’ll contribute directly to the successful delivery of projects, ensuring exceptional client experiences and reinforcing our position as a leading consultancy.
This role has been created to identify practical opportunities for AI and automation, support the rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot and related tools, and help develop internal solutions that make everyday work simpler, faster, and more consistent. You’ll work closely with colleagues across the business, gaining hands-on experience in applied AI, digital improvement, and change delivery.
As a wholly owned subsidiary of North Yorkshire Council, we’re one of the largest and most respected building design consultancies in the North of England. Our collaborative, forward-thinking team delivers a wide range of services, including:
As a Graduate AI & Automation Analyst, working closely with colleagues in the Technology and Change team at North Yorkshire Council and with department leads, you’ll support the identification, testing, and rollout of AI tools, internal agents, and automated workflows that deliver real business value. This is a development role designed to help you build capability through practical experimentation, guided delivery, and collaboration with experienced professionals, external specialists, and our AI working group.
You’ll focus on how AI can be used responsibly and effectively in a professional services environment, helping teams reduce repetitive tasks, improve quality, and make better use of knowledge and data to improve service and project delivery for all our clients.
The type of early work you may be involved in includes helping to build internal AI tools that support quality assurance of technical documents, structure photographic and survey evidence into draft outputs for review, compare contractor quotations against agreed schedules or benchmarks, and identify inconsistencies or omissions in project information so these can be checked by qualified staff.
Experience with AI tools, Copilot, automation, scripting, or digital projects is welcome, but enthusiasm, logic, and a willingness to learn are just as important.
When you join Align, you will join a team of professionals who feel rewarded for the work they do. Operating in a friendly and professional environment, we want to provide the training and resources to succeed and thrive in your role. Our people are not just numbers, everyone is crucial to the vital services we provide, and we treat everyone in our teams with respect and complete support.
In return for your commitment, we offer:
This role is ideal for someone at the start of their career who wants to build practical, future-facing digital skills while making a visible impact in a professional consultancy environment!

Career progression and professional development opportunities.

summary_intro:
Wernick are specialists in the design and construction of temporary and permanent modular buildings, delivering sophisticated, sustainable offsite solutions that combine speed with architectural quality.
With a proud history dating back to 1934, the Wernick Group has grown to become Britain’s largest independent manufacturer and hirer of portable and modular accommodation, and we’re not slowing down.
We are now looking for a driven, ambitious, and commercially minded Graduate Commercial Executive to join our growing team. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone eager to build a career in sales, gain exposure to major projects, and play a key role in shaping how we engage with our customers.
This is not just a support role, it’s your launchpad into a commercial career. You’ll be at the centre of our sales operation, working closely with the Head of Sales and wider team to drive performance, improve processes, and support the delivery of high-quality bids and customer experiences.
If you enjoy the buzz of sales, are eager to learn, and want to develop a long-term career in a commercial or sales role, this is your opportunity to make an impact from day one. This may be your first role after finishing university, so if you have the right attitude, work ethos, and know your way around a computer, we can teach you the rest.
It’s not necessarily about experience, we’re looking for attitude, energy, and potential.
At Wernick, you're more than an employee; you're a vital part of a team that’s building the future of construction. Join us in our journey of continuous innovation and commitment to quality, and let's be 'Altogether Stronger'.
We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all sections of the community. We thank you in advance for your interest in this role and our company.
As a family-owned and operated business since our inception, we blend traditional values with a forward-looking approach. This unique combination ensures a work environment that respects legacy while embracing the future.
Our expansive operations, with 40 centres across 36 UK locations, offer a vast array of roles and career paths in the public and private sectors. From modular building solutions to off-grid power, your professional journey can be as dynamic and varied as our services.
At Wernick, excellence isn’t just a goal; it's our way of life. We pride ourselves on providing outstanding product quality and service, creating an environment where your work directly contributes to customer satisfaction and business success.
We believe in nurturing talent from within. Through ongoing training and development opportunities, we invest in your future, ensuring that your career at Wernick is not just a job, but a journey of growth and learning.
Our business model is streamlined to reduce bureaucracy, enabling you to work in an environment that values decisiveness and efficiency. This approach allows you to focus on what you do best, without unnecessary complications.
We're committed to reducing our carbon footprint and ensuring a safe, positive working environment. Working with us means being part of a team that cares for the planet and its people.

what_youll_do:
Wernick are specialists in the design and construction of temporary and permanent modular buildings, delivering sophisticated, sustainable offsite solutions that combine speed with architectural quality.
With a proud history dating back to 1934, the Wernick Group has grown to become Britain’s largest independent manufacturer and hirer of portable and modular accommodation, and we’re not slowing down.
We are now looking for a driven, ambitious, and commercially minded Graduate Commercial Executive to join our growing team. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone eager to build a career in sales, gain exposure to major projects, and play a key role in shaping how we engage with our customers.
This is not just a support role, it’s your launchpad into a commercial career. You’ll be at the centre of our sales operation, working closely with the Head of Sales and wider team to drive performance, improve processes, and support the delivery of high-quality bids and customer experiences.
If you enjoy the buzz of sales, are eager to learn, and want to develop a long-term career in a commercial or sales role, this is your opportunity to make an impact from day one. This may be your first role after finishing university, so if you have the right attitude, work ethos, and know your way around a computer, we can teach you the rest.
It’s not necessarily about experience, we’re looking for attitude, energy, and potential.
At Wernick, you're more than an employee; you're a vital part of a team that’s building the future of construction. Join us in our journey of continuous innovation and commitment to quality, and let's be 'Altogether Stronger'.
We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all sections of the community. We thank you in advance for your interest in this role and our company.
As a family-owned and operated business since our inception, we blend traditional values with a forward-looking approach. This unique combination ensures a work environment that respects legacy while embracing the future.
Our expansive operations, with 40 centres across 36 UK locations, offer a vast array of roles and career paths in the public and private sectors. From modular building solutions to off-grid power, your professional journey can be as dynamic and varied as our services.
At Wernick, excellence isn’t just a goal; it's our way of life. We pride ourselves on providing outstanding product quality and service, creating an environment where your work directly contributes to customer satisfaction and business success.
We believe in nurturing talent from within. Through ongoing training and development opportunities, we invest in your future, ensuring that your career at Wernick is not just a job, but a journey of growth and learning.
Our business model is streamlined to reduce bureaucracy, enabling you to work in an environment that values decisiveness and efficiency. This approach allows you to focus on what you do best, without unnecessary complications.
We're committed to reducing our carbon footprint and ensuring a safe, positive working environment. Working with us means being part of a team that cares for the planet and its people.

summary_intro:
At Symphony Talent, we help our 900+ clients worldwide connect with people in ways that matter. We combine insight, creativity and technology to build employer brands that attract, engage and retain talent - and we do it with people firmly at the centre.
The Studio at Symphony Talent is where our strategy comes to life - turning insight into bold ideas, and ideas into work that shows up across the entire candidate journey. Client Managers play a key role here, helping translate client needs into clear direction for creative teams, and keeping work moving smoothly from brief to delivery. Everything we do is backed by our tech and media capabilities, so our work doesn’t just look good, it delivers real results.
With teams across New York, London, Bangalore and Belfast, we work globally, with a hands-on, collaborative culture that values curiosity, ownership and learning.
As a Graduate Client Manager, you’ll take your first step into client management within a creative studio environment. You’ll support our Client Management team by helping keep projects moving, clients informed, and teams aligned.
Alongside client work, you’ll also get involved in Studio-led initiatives that elevate Symphony Talent’s creative presence in the market - from case studies to thought leadership and internal projects.
This role is ideal for someone curious, organised and eager to build a career in client services or account management within a creative studio environment.
Help keep client projects moving, supporting day-to-day communication, coordinating requests and making sure everyone’s aligned.
Track progress, support resourcing and scheduling, flag issues early, and help keep projects organised and on track.
Get involved in Studio-led content and initiatives, working with Marketing to help bring our work and culture to life.
Build a strong understanding of our clients and brands, while learning how employer branding work gets planned, delivered and measured.
Learn how creative work is scoped, budgeted and tracked, and support the team in spotting opportunities to work smarter.
Work closely with teams across the Studio, contribute to a positive, collaborative culture, and bring fresh thinking to problem-solving.
This role is open to candidates with the right to work in the UK. Symphony Talent is committed to equality of opportunity in employment.
If you’re excited about building strong relationships, learning how great work gets delivered, and growing your career in a creative studio environment, we’d love to hear from you.

At Symphony Talent, we help our 900+ clients worldwide connect with people in ways that matter. We combine insight, creativity and technology to build employer brands that attract, engage and retain talent - and we do it with people firmly at the centre.
The Studio at Symphony Talent is where our strategy comes to life - turning insight into bold ideas, and ideas into work that shows up across the entire candidate journey. Client Managers play a key role here, helping translate client needs into clear direction for creative teams, and keeping work moving smoothly from brief to delivery. Everything we do is backed by our tech and media capabilities, so our work doesn’t just look good, it delivers real results.
With teams across New York, London, Bangalore and Belfast, we work globally, with a hands-on, collaborative culture that values curiosity, ownership and learning.
As a Graduate Client Manager, you’ll take your first step into client management within a creative studio environment. You’ll support our Client Management team by helping keep projects moving, clients informed, and teams aligned.
Alongside client work, you’ll also get involved in Studio-led initiatives that elevate Symphony Talent’s creative presence in the market - from case studies to thought leadership and internal projects.
This role is ideal for someone curious, organised and eager to build a career in client services or account management within a creative studio environment.
Help keep client projects moving, supporting day-to-day communication, coordinating requests and making sure everyone’s aligned.
Track progress, support resourcing and scheduling, flag issues early, and help keep projects organised and on track.

Build a strong understanding of our clients and brands, while learning how employer branding work gets planned, delivered and measured.

Work closely with teams across the Studio, contribute to a positive, collaborative culture, and bring fresh thinking to problem-solving.

If you’re excited about building strong relationships, learning how great work gets delivered, and growing your career in a creative studio environment, we’d love to hear from you.

summary_intro:
RSK Geosciences is recruiting for a Graduate Geo-Environmental Engineer to join the team based in Newcastle, UK . This is a full-time, permanent position.
We are a market-leading site investigation, contaminated land and geotechnical consultancy with geophysics and survey teams and waste management consultants, operating from 20 UK locations. Our company also includes Leap Environmental, an award-winning site investigation, geotechnical design and geoenvironmental consultancy, and Carbon Zero Consulting, which undertakes appraisals for ground source heat projects.
Throughout our 30 years of operations, we have enabled our clients to realise opportunities and manage the potential liabilities associated with acquiring, owning, operating and developing land. Our clients come from the public and private sectors, including many of the UK’s leading property developers, major and local house builders, utility providers and main contractors, local authorities and other government organisations.
RSK Geosciences is part of the RSK Group, a leading integrated environmental, engineering, and technical services business providing dynamic, multidisciplinary services to a wide range of sectors. RSK was founded in 1989 and has grown considerably since then.
At RSK, we operate as a group of businesses that work together seamlessly, aiming for growth through diversification. Our strategy helps us build a strong and resilient business, capable of weathering external challenges, while also providing greater value to our clients and more opportunities for our employees.
Since the beginning, our philosophy has remained the same: employ, develop and reward talented individuals. People are crucial to our company, and we recognise that our success hinges on our colleagues' growth. We're committed to preserving RSK's people-first culture, promoting innovation, and fostering a supportive and caring environment for collaboration. At RSK, we want you to be part of our successes and help you reach your career aspirations. We take pride in offering employees fulfilling and challenging careers by promoting ongoing growth and empowering individuals to excel.
We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that welcomes individuals from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We firmly believe that embracing and celebrating the diversity in our workforce makes us a stronger and more innovative company.
By providing workplace adjustments, we make it easier for people to confidently explore and pursue our career opportunities and recognise that flexibility is key to fostering a dynamic and thriving workplace. Many of our office-based positions benefit from a flexible working arrangement, allowing our team members to achieve a balance between professional and personal commitments.
We actively encourage applications from candidates of all genders, races, ethnicities, ages, neurotypes, religions or beliefs, sexual orientations, and those with disabilities.
If you're passionate about making a difference, join us as we work together to build a brighter, more equitable, and sustainable future for all. Do you have what it takes?

summary_intro:
Join Our Team and Make a Difference!
Enjoy problem-solving and helping customers? Become a Pest Control Technician with Rentokil in England and Wales. Full training provided, no experience necessary. Apply now!
We are currently seeking a Pest Control Technician to join our dedicated team of travelling Technicians, covering England and Wales. If you enjoy managing your own schedule and solving unique customer problems in person, this could be the perfect opportunity for you!
Our Graduate Pest Control Technicians joining our specialist hit squad supporting key branches across the UK, working on service improvement. You will be working within different branches across the UK, therefore, a commitment to working and staying away from home during your working week is required. You'll provide effective solutions for residential and commercial pest control, including rodent control, insect control, and bird control, ensuring excellent customer service while resolving pest problems.
You'll start as a Graduate Pest Control Technician, gaining invaluable frontline experience over 6-12 months. You'll receive world-class, industry-recognised training leading to a globally respected Pest Control Qualification – a valuable asset for your entire career! Key responsibilities include:
This travelling role offers unparalleled networking opportunities and typically leads to progression. After mastering your skills, the next 12-36 months unlock exciting opportunities to shape your own future within Rentokil Initial. Our structured development programme provides progression opportunities into diverse roles such as:
Rentokil offers you the platform to follow your own career path while constantly learning on the job and developing your career.
Be Yourself in Your Application!
At Rentokil Initial, we value innovation, but we want to see the real you! While AI can help with structure and grammar, make sure your application shows your true passion and understanding of the role. A personal touch will help you stand out.
A Company Putting “People First”
Rentokil Initial (FTSE100) is one of the largest business services companies in the world, operating in over 90 countries and providing services that protect people and enhance lives. Rentokil is the world’s leading commercial pest control services provider, Initial is the world’s leading commercial hygiene services provider, and Ambius is the world’s leading provider of plants and scenting.
As a business, we focus on the Right People, doing the Right Things, and in the Right Way. We invest a lot of time and money in training and developing all our colleagues to be the best they can be, and we are always looking for talented and driven people to join our Rentokil Initial Family.
Rentokil Initial are an equal opportunities employer and are committed to creating a diverse working environment.

Join the core of the Quick Release business, delivering smart solutions to data driven problems.
Have the opportunity to become an expert in particular fields, sharing knowledge and training others.
Building long-term relationships with clients and making a meaningful impact on projects.
Complete first-class induction training, then continue your learning through working with industry-leading talent on real, client-facing projects.
Work alongside client teams (on location) to understand their challenges, then use your expertise to find and deliver technical solutions to help them get new products to market faster, more efficiently and more sustainably.
Develop technical product data management expertise and systematically address and improve the way these clients manage their product data - solving problems and shaping solutions to deliver the right outcomes.
Experience a range of projects, businesses, sectors, and workplaces, getting to know and understand how our clients operate.
Develop strong trusting relationships with clients and team-mates.
Support deployments and development of our technical/software tools and solutions.

A first-class or high 2:1 bachelor’s degree, master's degree or PhD in any discipline (it doesn’t need to be STEM).
Emerging people and project management skills and the drive to take on responsibility - determination to be the best and genuinely make things better.
Strong communication skills, accompanied by self-awareness and emotional intelligence. You enjoy helping people.
The ability to make sense of complexity and present compelling data-driven stories and solutions that resonate with stakeholders.
A starting salary of £33,000 plus other rewards and benefits.
A highly motivated, diverse, talented and supportive team with a positive, people-focused company culture.
Extensive induction training and ongoing learning and development.
Projects with a variety of clients, locations and workplaces, all with real-world impact.
Career progression based on merit and a choice of pathways.
Lots of team events, sports clubs, CSR, mental health, diversity and well-being initiatives, and a direct line to management and leadership for your ideas.
The knowledge, skills and experience to ensure you'll always be in demand, wherever your career may take you.

So, whether you've just finished university, you're returning to work after time out, or you're looking for a new challenge in a new sector, the ongoing growth of our team means we have opportunities to join QR throughout the year.
Some projects will be challenging, but they will always be rewarding, and you’ll be surrounded by a team of talented people who will support you all the way! To make things easier for you, the application form allows you to specify which location(s) you want to apply to, so you only need to apply once. Please note that you will be expected to work from your assigned client site/regional office up to five days per week.
As an equal opportunities employer, Quick Release will never discriminate on the basis of gender, race, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, age, socio-economic background, marital status, or disability status.

If at any point throughout the recruitment process you require any reasonable adjustments to be made, please do let us know and we will be happy to help.
We're aware that many candidates these days are using AI language models to help them with their job applications. Whilst we understand the use of this kind of technology to assist with applications, it's worth noting that answers copied directly from AI tend to come across very generic and detract from the quality of applications. To give yourself the best chance of letting yourself shine in your application, we strongly recommend personalising your answers based on your own skills and experience.
This role may require you to have or be willing to go through National Security Vetting. As part of the onboarding process candidates will be asked to complete a Baseline Personnel Security Standard; details of the evidence required to apply may be found on the government website. If you are unable to meet this and any associated criteria, then your employment may be delayed, or rejected. Details of this will be discussed with you at interview.

summary_intro:
At PerkinElmer, we design, manufacture and deliver advanced technology solutions which address the world's most critical human and environmental health and safety concerns. Our Environmental Health business develops analytical instrumentation and support services, all to protect the quality and sustainability of our environment. PerkinElmer transforms information into actions that improve our safety today and our world tomorrow.
In the Spectroscopy Research team at High Wycombe, we investigate emerging technologies in infrared, near-infrared and UV spectroscopy. We actively lead the development of next-generation instruments for materials characterization and offer expert technical support from cradle to grave.
This is an opportunity to play a full part in the design and development of the mechanical aspects on new, state-of-the-art prototype instruments. You would be developing designs for manufacture, building prototypes, and playing a role in verification and troubleshooting. The mechanical aspects of the products involve a mix of precision metal and plastic parts, castings, electro-mechanical sub-systems, as well as optical components. You will be working in a small team that mixes highly skilled and experienced scientists and engineers with fellow students.
As a Student Mechanical Engineer, you will assist in research and development projects conducted within the department. These projects may relate to the development and modification of functional prototype infrared spectroscopy instruments. You will also participate in root cause investigations into manufacturing issues and play a part in problem resolution. The work is likely to include:
Training on the use of relevant laboratory equipment and standard methods will be given and support given in the interpretation of results.
To qualify, you must have completed a minimum of 2 years of an undergraduate degree in Mechanical Engineering (or a related subject) at the start of the placement. You will be working towards achieving a 2:1 or above and looking to complete a 12 month placement as part of your degree.
To be successful you will need:
PerkinElmer at High Wycombe has a history of taking students for placement years and many have gone on to take permanent roles in the organisation. Students are given stimulating and interesting projects to work on that are of genuine value to the business.
Please apply by submitting a CV and a covering letter.
Interviews will be carried out as suitable CVs are received.
We regret we will not consider candidates who have already graduated for this role.

summary_intro:
The “new” PerkinElmer business, a newly independent company as of March 13, 2023, is a global analytical services and solutions provider with offerings including the leading OneSource Field and Laboratory services business that serve the biopharma, food, environmental, safety and applied end markets to accelerate scientific outcomes. Since 1937, PerkinElmer has served as a trusted partner in laboratory analysis and management and today complements its service offerings with a broad portfolio of atomic spectroscopy, molecular spectroscopy, and chromatography instruments, consumables, and reagents. With a dedicated team of more than 6,000 team members, the Company serves customers in more than 35 countries.
At PerkinElmer, we design, manufacture and deliver advanced technology solutions which address the world's most critical human and environmental health and safety concerns. Our Environmental Health business develops analytical instrumentation and support services, all to protect the quality and sustainability of our environment. PerkinElmer transforms information into actions that improve our safety today and our world tomorrow.
In the Spectroscopy Research team at High Wycombe, we investigate emerging technologies in infrared, near-infrared and UV spectroscopy. We actively lead the development of next generation instruments for materials characterisation and offer expert technical support from cradle to grave.
This is an opportunity to play a full part in the design and development of the electronics on new, state-of-the-art prototype instruments. You could be responsible for your own PCBs/sub-systems from feasibility and design through to debug, system integration, and customer demonstration. You will be working in a small team mixing highly skilled and experienced scientists and engineers with fellow students.
As a Student Electronic Engineer, you will assist in research and development projects conducted within the department. These projects may relate to the development and modification of functional prototype infrared spectroscopy instruments. The work is likely to include:
Several different projects will be available involving analogue circuit design for low signal amplification, design of high-performance closed loop control systems, digital signal processing, WiFi, and wireless communication.
Training on the use of relevant laboratory equipment and standard methods will be given and support provided in the interpretation of results.
To qualify, you must have completed a minimum of 2 years of an undergraduate degree in Electronic Engineering (or a related subject) at the start of the placement.
You will be working towards achieving a 2:1 or above and looking to complete a 12-month placement as part of your degree.
PerkinElmer at High Wycombe has a history of taking students for placement years and many have gone on to take permanent roles in the organisation. Students are given stimulating and interesting projects to work on that are of genuine value to the business.
Please apply with your CV and a covering letter outlining why you are interested in this opportunity. Applications will be reviewed as they arrive, and an appointment will be made as soon as a suitable candidate is identified.

summary_intro:
The “new” PerkinElmer business, a newly independent company as of March 13, 2023, is a global analytical services and solutions provider with offerings including the leading OneSource Field and Laboratory services business that serve the biopharma, food, environmental, safety and applied end markets to accelerate scientific outcomes. Since 1937, PerkinElmer has served as a trusted partner in laboratory analysis and management and today complements its service offerings with a broad portfolio of atomic spectroscopy, molecular spectroscopy, and chromatography instruments, consumables, and reagents. With a dedicated team of more than 6,000 team members, the Company serves customers in more than 35 countries.
At PerkinElmer, we design, manufacture and deliver advanced technology solutions which address the world's most critical human and environmental health and safety concerns. Our Environmental Health business develops analytical instrumentation and support services, all to protect the quality and sustainability of our environment. PerkinElmer transforms information into actions that improve our safety today and our world tomorrow.
In the Spectroscopy Research team at High Wycombe, we investigate emerging technologies in infrared, near-infrared and UV spectroscopy. We actively lead the development of next generation instruments for materials characterisation and offer expert technical support from cradle to grave.
This is an opportunity to play a full part in the design and development of the electronics on new, state-of-the-art prototype instruments. You could be responsible for your own PCBs/sub-systems from feasibility and design through to debug, system integration, and customer demonstration. You will be working in a small team mixing highly skilled and experienced scientists and engineers with fellow students.
As a Student Electronic Engineer, you will assist in research and development projects conducted within the department. These projects may relate to the development and modification of functional prototype infrared spectroscopy instruments. The work is likely to include:
Several different projects will be available involving analogue circuit design for low signal amplification, design of high-performance closed loop control systems, digital signal processing, WiFi, and wireless communication.
Training on the use of relevant laboratory equipment and standard methods will be given and support provided in the interpretation of results.
To qualify, you must have completed a minimum of 2 years of an undergraduate degree in Electronic Engineering (or a related subject) at the start of the placement.

requirement_summery:
Assist in the design and delivery of individual diet and nutrition programmes for players that aligns to the requirements of the Elite Player Performance Programme (EPPP).
Assist with insights of nutritional support for injury and rehabilitation programmes for adult and youth players, in conjunction with the Multi-Disciplinary Team (MDT).
Support with the implementation of innovative and evidence-based nutrition curriculum and education sessions and resources to increase nutrition knowledge throughout the Academy and Women’s levels for players, parents and colleagues.
In conjunction with the MDT, assist with player fitness and strength development, and body composition through nutritional interventions.
Work collaboratively with the MDT on the development of each player as part of the 6-12 weekly multidisciplinary review process.
Support match days as directed to assist/implement nutritional provision and provide post-game recovery support where appropriate.
Maintain records of all nutrition interventions and track measurable outcomes linked to nutritional practices (body composition, nutritional knowledge, anti-doping awareness, hydration etc.).
Work collaboratively with kitchen and catering staff to ensure adequate food service and provision aligning with nutritional requirements on training and match days.
Assist with relevant stock checks for supplements and provide updates for relevant orders.
A strong work ethic, meticulous attention to detail, and excellent communication skills are essential for this role alongside a willingness to learn and a passion for a career in the environment.
Be an Undergraduate student in the placement year of Nutrition, Sport and Exercise Science, Sports Nutrition, Dietetics or a similar course.
Due to the nature of the role, there is an expectation to be available to attend weekend and evening activity on a regular basis.
Final projects
Professional practice pieces
Contemporary research methods
Examining a professional environment
Independent research projects
£500 Contribution to living allowance per month
Opportunity to work in an elite environment
Learning and development opportunities through internal CPD
Breakfast and lunch included
Full club kit

summary_intro:
Right across infrastructure, there’s a requirement to not only maintain, but also renew and reimagine. Whatever stage you’re at in your career, with us you’ll have an opportunity to grow and develop. Delivering essential infrastructure services for life, while being safety first, and client and customer centric in a friendly, fun and respectful environment where you are encouraged to thrive.
At M Group Water we help our clients safeguard the water supply, improve environmental performance and manage demand for future generations. We enhance and extend asset life, ensuring compliance with water quality and environmental standards. We’re problem solvers with over 140 years of combined experience in engineering and infrastructure.
This role will join BGEN - one of the UK's largest multidisciplinary design and build contractors with over 100 years of industry experience. We support clients in the water, power & energy, pharmaceutical, nuclear and food and beverage industries to deliver next generation, value-added engineering solutions.
We have an exciting opportunity for an Operations Student Placement to join us for a 12-month Industrial Placement (September 2025 to August 2026), based primarily in Stafford, with occasional work from our Derby and Warrington offices. This is a great opportunity for someone currently studying for a degree in Business, Economics or Finance and seeking hands-on experience in industry.
Our one-year industrial placement is incredibly flexible, offering you experience of many different aspects of a large national engineering business. You will be working closely with the Operations and Engineering teams, but you will also interact with other stakeholders in the business such as project managers and the commercial team. You will develop a good understanding of business operations and how we deliver and manage our projects. This role will be the perfect opportunity for a student hoping to get a varied and rich first experience in business operations, through being completely embedded into the team and processes.
We offer a range of benefits designed to support your life in and out of work, some of which include:
We want to be an employer of choice and a great place to work, attracting diverse and talented people, who join us and make a difference. We’re one of the Top 100 UK companies actively supporting and recruiting army veterans. Our ENABLE inclusion networks bring together people who have a shared passion, to help create an environment where everyone belongs.
Our values help to shape our culture and how we work with one another. We recruit with these values in mind, to ensure your aspirations, and ways of working, align with ours.
Whether you’re a trainee, apprentice or graduate, or progressing through your career, our people benefit from industry recognised programmes, training and development.
It’s an exceptional time to be a part of M Group.
Please note: Occasionally, job adverts might be closed before the stated closing date. Do apply as soon as possible to ensure your application is considered.
For certain roles, successful candidates will be subject to 3rd party background checks as part of the hiring process.

summary_intro:
Fleming-Agri Products have an exciting placement opportunity for a Student Engineer commencing in September 2025. Fleming Agri Products is a leading manufacturer of agricultural machinery based in Newbuildings, Northern Ireland. The company promotes a value for money product portfolio that is sold extensively throughout the UK, Ireland, and several significant export markets including France, and New Zealand. All manufacturing facilities are sited in Newbuildings with metal processing and finishing the primary activities.
As a Student Engineer, you will support the engineering department and work closely with our production team to design and develop both existing and new products. This is an exciting opportunity for a student engineer to undertake their placement in the manufacturing/engineering sector.
Undertake any additional duties as required to improve product and process efficiency.
To be eligible for this role, you must currently hold a right to work in the UK
Fleming Agri Products is an equal opportunity employer
The Fleming Agri factory is based in Newbuildings, North West Northern Ireland. The purpose built factory was established in 1983 on a modest half acre site. Over the years the factory has had several expansion developments including a £1.1m expansion which was completed in 2013. More recently a new 22,000 square feet factory has been opened mid 2020 for the manufacture of larger capacity trailers and vacuum tankers.
With the pace of new technology moving so fast, the company embraces a policy of continuous improvement, involving the most up to date design packages, CNC production machinery and processes including robotic welding.
All Fleming products are designed and manufactured with our motto “Simplicity is our Strength” in mind.
Here at Fleming Agri we aim to manufacture products with a strong, simple design, making them easy to operate and run while offering sufficient strength for their given purpose.
Our products are customer focused with research and design carried out by our in-house engineering team who continually work to a standard that has the end-user’s satisfaction in mind.
All new products are extensively tested throughout the design and development process to ensure the customer has quality and strength in the product and a value for money machine as the end result.
At Fleming Agri, we are always on the lookout for new employees to join our team.
If you have drive and ambition to work hard, in what can often be a challenging environment, Fleming Agri want to hear from you.
We offer competitive packages for all our staff.

Support Product Managers with analysis of user behaviour, engagement, retention, and feature performance.
Assist in defining, tracking, and reporting on core product KPIs across divisions.
Build and maintain dashboards and reports to provide clear visibility of product and performance metrics.
Analyse trends and variances against targets or forecasts, identifying risks and opportunities.
Support experimentation and A/B testing by gathering, analysing, and interpreting results.
Work closely with Engineering and Data colleagues to ensure data accuracy and integrity.
Contribute to the standardisation of product and performance reporting frameworks.
Conduct ad hoc analysis to support roadmap decisions and strategic initiatives.
Translate complex data into clear, concise insights suitable for both operational and senior stakeholders.
Ensure all data handling complies with UK GDPR and internal governance standards.
Demonstrate flexibility and a willingness to learn across functions, with potential opportunities over time to gain broader exposure across Product, Development and Engineering teams as part of the graduate development pathway.
Participate in cross-functional discussions to understand divisional objectives and align data insight accordingly.
Recent graduate in Data Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Business Analytics, or similar analytical discipline.
Strong numerical and analytical capability.
High proficiency in Excel (including formulas, pivot tables, data manipulation).
Ability to structure data and draw logical, evidence-based conclusions.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and methodical approach to problem-solving.
Curiosity about digital products and how data informs decision-making.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, evolving technology environment.
Exposure to SQL and/or data querying tools.
Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or other BI platforms.
Understanding of product performance metrics (e.g., conversion, retention, engagement, churn).
Awareness of digital product lifecycle and agile methodologies.
Basic understanding of commercial and operational performance indicators.
Knowledge of data governance and data protection principles.

summary_intro:
DigitalKOG is looking for a Graduate or Junior Graphic Designer to join our creative marketing team in Preston. We welcome applications from ambitious designers with strong creative potential and a genuine enthusiasm for design. We are looking for someone with a natural creative flair who enjoys developing ideas and creating engaging design work for our home improvement clients.
At DigitalKOG, we keep the end user at the centre of every piece of creative. Our focus is on producing work that helps attract customers and supports real business growth. We believe that creativity without results has limited value, so we measure success by the impact our work has on performance as well as how it looks.
Our creative approach is always evolving. We continually refine our design output to stay responsive to changing trends, audience behaviour and the wider marketing landscape. Every piece of work is rooted in a clear understanding of each client and their brand strategy, so we are looking for someone who is ready to embrace that mindset and develop a strong sense of creative purpose.
In this role, you will benefit from direct mentorship from our Creative Director and Senior Creative Designer. You will work across a wide range of projects, helping to turn campaign concepts into effective creative content across multiple marketing channels. This will include concept development, front-end web design, email marketing, social content creation, and creative copywriting. You will also have the opportunity to work closely with the wider creative team while collaborating with our experienced marketing specialists.
The successful candidate will have experience using Adobe Creative Suite. Agency experience or a relevant placement would be beneficial, but it is not essential.
Our team members work incredibly hard and we like to reward them for that. So, on top of receiving a competitive salary, we'll also treat you to a yearly bonus when you help us achieve our ambitions. You will be given the freedom to shape the future direction of our agency. All ideas are welcomed and listened to as we know that our people drive our success and we want everyone to be a part of that.
We have our own dedicated office space, where we love collaborating together, with lots of FREE private parking available. The office is brilliantly located, close to the motorway for simple commuting, with a retail park just across the road – fancy a Burger King, Costa or Greggs for lunch?
DigitalKOG very much feels like a family and we all love getting out after work, whether it’s going to the local micropub or heading into town for a curry.
We know that agency life can be very fast-paced and how important it is for our team members to have time out from that to recharge the batteries. So, we offer 30 days’ holiday, PLUS bank holidays, including a total shutdown over the Christmas break – not many agencies can compete with that. To help you get financially prepared for life after work, you will also be enrolled onto a competitive pension scheme.
We are firmly committed to enhancing your personal and professional development, providing 1-2-1 coaching and mentoring programs, team workshops, and soft skills training, overseen by our resident Development Coach, Charlotte Haslam. There will also be dedicated learning days as we take knowledge sharing seriously, with in-house training programs, innovation days, and opportunities to get involved in 3rd party training all available. We’ll also support you in furthering your learning outside of work.
Supporting the mental health of our team is a major priority for us. We run a series of initiatives to develop team relationships and keep everyone’s mental wellbeing strong.

title: Graduate Account Specialist
listing_snippet:
Location: Wilmslow (office based)
Salary/package: £28,000 per annum plus commission
Hours: Full time, 37 hours per week
If you are a recent graduate who enjoys working with people, building relationships and delivering great service, this is an opportunity to start a career in recruitment while making a genuine difference to students across the UK.
Impact Student Partners is part of Commercial Services Group (CSG) , the UK’s largest local authority owned trading company. Impact Student Partners
summary_intro:
Location: Wilmslow (office based)
Salary/package: £28,000 per annum plus commission
Hours: Full time, 37 hours per week
If you are a recent graduate who enjoys working with people, building relationships and delivering great service, this is an opportunity to start a career in recruitment while making a genuine difference to students across the UK.
Impact Student Partners is part of Commercial Services Group (CSG) , the UK’s largest local authority owned trading company. Impact Student Partners specialises in placing tutors, mentors, and specialist support workers into higher education settings, helping students with disabilities succeed at university. As a CSG business, our commercial success directly supports social value and reinvestment into public services.
As a Graduate Account Specialist, you will play a key role in supporting universities and students by matching them with the right specialist support professionals. This is a relationship‑driven role, similar to an account manager position, with a strong focus on customer service, organisation, and communication.
You will manage relationships with students, candidates and university partners, building trust and ensuring a high‑quality experience throughout the recruitment process. While previous recruitment experience is not required, an interest in recruitment and a desire to develop commercial skills is essential.
Commercial Services Group (CSG) is the UK’s largest local authority-owned trading company (LATCO), generating over £800 million in revenue and supporting 16,000 education and public sector customers worldwide. With more than 1,800 employees across the UK, France, Dubai, and Bangkok, we are working towards becoming the global leader in education and public sector solutions.
We are expanding rapidly, with annual growth of around 25 percent, supported by a blend of organic development, acquisitions and strategic partnerships. Our 33 trading businesses deliver a wide range of services including education management, IT, HR, legal, energy, procurement, and supplies.
CSG is wholly owned by local authorities, and a significant proportion of our profits is reinvested into frontline public services. Over £77 million has already been returned, reflecting our commitment to combining commercial performance with meaningful social impact.
We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. We encourage applications from suitably qualified people of all backgrounds.
We are committed to providing reasonable adjustments throughout our application and interview process; please let us know if you require any.

summary_intro:
At CloserStill, we strive to deliver the best. Our mission is to be the most dynamic B2B events and communities business in every market we serve - bringing people together to learn, connect and grow.
Applications are now open for our 2026 Graduate Bootcamp.
If you’re ambitious, curious and ready to launch your career at one of the world’s leading events businesses, this is your moment.
Our Graduate Bootcamp is a 10-week paid programme designed to give you real experience, real skills and real momentum. You’ll rotate across key departments, learn from industry leaders and finish with the commercial understanding and confidence to build a serious career in events.
And it works. Over 17% of our current London workforce began their journey on a previous Bootcamp. This is not a summer placement. It is a launchpad into a long-term career at a company that invests in its people.
Over 10 weeks, you’ll be immersed in CloserStill Media - rotating across departments, contributing to live projects and learning what it truly takes to deliver some of the world’s most successful B2B events.
You will not stay on the sidelines. We want to give you the platform to contribute from day one.
At the end of the programme, all grads will have the opportunity to apply and interview for a permanent role at CloserStill Media. Interview skills and preparation form part of the journey, so you will be fully equipped when that opportunity comes.
This is a paid role with a competitive starting salary.
The Bootcamp rotates across five core areas of the business, giving you a broad and commercially grounded understanding of how a world-class events company operates.
Operations make our events happen. Every floorplan, build, speaker session, stage set-up and piece of AV is planned and executed by this team.
It is fast-paced, detail-driven and deadline-focused. You’ll learn how complex live environments are delivered seamlessly - and why precision matters.
Marketing drives audience and exhibitor growth across our portfolio. Using a mix of paid digital, email, partnerships and creative campaigns, the team communicates the value of attending and exhibiting with clarity and impact. You’ll see how strategy, data and creativity combine to drive measurable commercial results.
Content defines the credibility of our events. Our Content teams are industry specialists who research markets, identify trends and secure the world-class speakers that shape each programme. You’ll learn how authority is built, how insight becomes agenda-setting content and how strong programming drives commercial success.
This rotation is centred on Digital Marketing, where you’ll drive campaign performance, customer acquisition and audience growth across paid media, email, social media, content and automation. You’ll also spend time with our Technology team, gaining exposure to the product strategy, CX systems and platforms that power registration, CRM, event apps and data across our portfolio.
New for 2026, this dedicated Sprint fast-tracks your development. You’ll begin with focused professional training designed to strengthen core workplace skills and commercial awareness. You’ll then work directly with our Learning & Development and Communications teams — contributing to live initiatives, understanding how training programmes are built and rolled out, and seeing how communication shapes culture and performance across an international business. This rotation blends structured learning with real responsibility, building the transferable skills that set future leaders apart.
You don't need to have it all figured out, but you do need the right mindset. We're looking for people who are:
Shortlisting: You will be notified in early March whether you have secured a place at the assessment days.
Assessment Days: 31st March or 9th April 2026, in person at our Global HQ in Hammersmith, London. You will need to attend in person on one of these days; please keep both dates free until you receive confirmation of your slot.
Bootcamp Dates: 6th July 2026 – 11th September 2026 (subject to change)
Location: Full in-office attendance at our Hammersmith HQ is required for the duration of the Bootcamp.
Salary: This is a paid role with a competitive starting salary.
CloserStill Media embraces diversity in all its forms and is committed to continuing to develop a diverse and inclusive environment that encourages collaboration and innovation.
We are an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment based on merit without attention to age, ethnicity, religion or beliefs, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, or disability status.
We are committed to ensuring an inclusive and accessible recruitment process.

At the end of the programme, all grads will have the opportunity to apply and interview for a permanent role at CloserStill Media. Interview skills and preparation form part of the journey, so you will be fully equipped when that opportunity comes.
This is a paid role with a competitive starting salary.
The Bootcamp rotates across five core areas of the business, giving you a broad and commercially grounded understanding of how a world-class events company operates.
Operations make our events happen. Every floorplan, build, speaker session, stage set-up and piece of AV is planned and executed by this team.
It is fast-paced, detail-driven and deadline-focused. You’ll learn how complex live environments are delivered seamlessly - and why precision matters.
Marketing drives audience and exhibitor growth across our portfolio. Using a mix of paid digital, email, partnerships and creative campaigns, the team communicates the value of attending and exhibiting with clarity and impact. You’ll see how strategy, data and creativity combine to drive measurable commercial results.
Content defines the credibility of our events. Our Content teams are industry specialists who research markets, identify trends and secure the world-class speakers that shape each programme. You’ll learn how authority is built, how insight becomes agenda-setting content and how strong programming drives commercial success.
This rotation is centred on Digital Marketing, where you’ll drive campaign performance, customer acquisition and audience growth across paid media, email, social media, content and automation. You’ll also spend time with our Technology team, gaining exposure to the product strategy, CX systems and platforms that power registration, CRM, event apps and data across our portfolio.
New for 2026, this dedicated Sprint fast-tracks your development. You’ll begin with focused professional training designed to strengthen core workplace skills and commercial awareness. You’ll then work directly with our Learning & Development and Communications teams — contributing to live initiatives, understanding how training programmes are built and rolled out, and seeing how communication shapes culture and performance across an international business. This rotation blends structured learning with real responsibility, building the transferable skills that set future leaders apart.
You don't need to have it all figured out, but you do need the right mindset. We're looking for people who are:
Shortlisting: You will be notified in early March whether you have secured a place at the assessment days.
Assessment Days: 31st March or 9th April 2026, in person at our Global HQ in Hammersmith, London. You will need to attend in person on one of these days; please keep both dates free until you receive confirmation of your slot.
Bootcamp Dates: 6th July 2026 – 11th September 2026 (subject to change)
Location: Full in-office attendance at our Hammersmith HQ is required for the duration of the Bootcamp.
Salary: This is a paid role with a competitive starting salary.

We are an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment based on merit without attention to age, ethnicity, religion or beliefs, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, or disability status.
We are committed to ensuring an inclusive and accessible recruitment process.

summary_intro:
As a graduate, we truly believe that you have what it takes to shape the future of the property industry. This means that you’ll be given real challenges and responsibility, right from the get-go. During our two-year programme, you’ll develop much more than just the technical skills needed to thrive in your field. You will develop leadership qualities which will help you to energise those around you and fast-track your career.
As a graduate in our Valuation team, you’ll join us on a two-year journey to become a Chartered Valuation Surveyor & registered valuer with the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS). You will have the opportunity to work on a range of real estate from industrial, offices, and retail through to large residential portfolios. We carry out Valuations for secured lending on behalf of a range of lenders as well as pension funds, financial statements and the public sector. At the same time, we’ll support you in completing your assessment of professional competence (APC) with involvement with other disciplines such as agency, lease advisory and property management.
We value graduates who aren’t afraid to step up and change the game. With that in mind, we’re looking for:

You will work collaboratively with colleagues in UKSRO to support the dynamic needs of events across the university calendar, preparing presentations about your time at university and key tips for new students. As part of our recruitment activities, you will attend UCAS exhibitions and careers fairs across the country, promoting and representing Bath Spa University.
With our events team you will assist in the planning and delivery of key university recruitment events such as open days, offer holder days, campus tours, and school visits, whilst monitoring the effectiveness of your contribution and providing information to colleagues based on insights and learnings from your time speaking with prospective students.
You will also contribute to the planning, organisation, and delivery of aspiration and attainment-raising outreach and transition programmes that support the University’s effective Access and Participation Plan.
(This is an 18 Month Full-Time Fixed Term Role)
Having graduated from Bath Spa University in 2025 (or being due to graduate before September 2026), you will have recent administrative experience covering a wide range of activities/services and be confident in a customer-facing role. We are looking for someone passionate about university recruitment and outreach, so experience working on events or supporting young people is important.
Being able to communicate clearly is key: you will need to be able to communicate effectively both internally and with external partners in a variety of mediums. You will also need to be confident in communicating through a variety of methods, including face to face, email, and over the phone.
Our busy events diary can include weekend and evening work, as well as visiting schools not accessible by public transport, so a willingness to travel and a full UK driving license are essential.
For further information on the essential and desirable skills we’re looking for, please refer to the attached Job Description.

Creative Technologists express creativity through engaging and innovative experiences, using the latest technologies and advancements. The Graduate Creative Technologist will work alongside members of academic staff to advance the progressive use of technologies in the School of Design and across creative subjects in other schools. Work will include research into new technologies, development of prototypes and learning materials based on these technologies, supporting student and staff projects, and authoring reports and presentations evaluating various services, tools, and technologies that Computing programmes could invest in.
Over time, graduates take on greater autonomy to plan and run projects, contribute in varying capacities where value can be added, as well as propose new projects and activities.
The graduate will also be a key junior associate in the newly created Centre for Creative Technology (CCT) within the School of Design, where they will work collaboratively and autonomously on a range of projects sourced from industry, research grants, and in response to developments in the wider technology sector. (This is an 18 Month Full Time Fixed Term Role)
The ideal candidate for Graduate Creative Technologist will have a strong and balanced blend of computing, creative, and problem-solving skills. It starts with excellent critical thinking and analysis skills, enabling a deep understanding of the problems to be solved before reaching conclusions on the solutions or approaches.
You will be able to work well with other people from different backgrounds and at different levels. You are also self-motivated, able to set your own tasks, and manage them to timely completion when working independently. You can communicate clearly and effectively, and are capable of organising information to meet the needs of your audience. Likewise, you are responsive to new information and welcome direction and feedback that helps you learn and grow.
Technical competence and skills are a strength, focused in particular around modern technologies used to plan, design, and express creativity. Skills will include but are not limited to development of websites, application software, graphics, and audio.
You will also have perseverance and adaptability, able to readily learn new tools and technologies as different needs emerge with each new project.

Creative Technologists express creativity through engaging and innovative experiences, using the latest technologies and advancements. The Graduate Creative Technologist will work alongside members of academic staff to advance the progressive use of technologies in the School of Design and across creative subjects in other schools. Work will include research into new technologies, development of prototypes and learning materials based on these technologies, supporting student and staff projects, and authoring reports and presentations evaluating various services, tools, and technologies that Computing programmes could invest in.
Over time, graduates take on greater autonomy to plan and run projects, contribute in varying capacities where value can be added, as well as propose new projects and activities.
The graduate will also be a key junior associate in the newly created Centre for Creative Technology (CCT) within the School of Design, where they will work collaboratively and autonomously on a range of projects sourced from industry, research grants, and in response to developments in the wider technology sector. It starts with excellent critical thinking and analysis skills, enabling a deep understanding of the problems to be solved before reaching conclusions on the solutions or approaches.
You will be able to work well with other people from different backgrounds and at different levels. You are also self-motivated, able to set your own tasks, and manage them to timely completion when working independently. You can communicate clearly and effectively, and are capable of organising information to meet the needs of your audience. Likewise, you are responsive to new information and welcome direction and feedback that helps you learn and grow.
Technical competence and skills are a strength, focused in particular around modern technologies used to plan, design, and express creativity. Skills will include but are not limited to development of websites, application software, graphics, and audio.
You will also have perseverance and adaptability, able to readily learn new tools and technologies as different needs emerge with each new project.

As of April 2024, there has been a change in the UK’s sponsorship threshold. Regrettably, as the salary for this role falls beneath this, you will not be eligible for sponsorship; therefore, your application will automatically be rejected.
The role will consist of assisting in the further development of the Student Digital Learning Assistant (SDLA) service. The SDLAs provide first line support for students in their use of digital tools by promoting and supporting the effective use of the University’s online services, systems and software.
The graduate will help manage the SDLAs by organising training, preparing rotas, and contributing to wider project work aimed at increasing engagement with the service. This will involve marketing (particularly at our Locksbrook campus), generating social media content, producing promotional videos and assisting with event planning and organisation.
The graduate will also help expand the reach of the service by developing asynchronous digital skills resources. Additionally, there will be opportunities to survey students, evaluate the current service and propose ideas for further improvement.
(This is a 18 Month Full Time Fixed Term Role)
The ideal graduate will be personally interested in the student experience at BSU and motivated to help enhance students’ digital knowledge and confidence. Excellent customer service and communication skills are essential, as the role involves working closely with students, supporting the SDLA team, and collaborating with colleagues across the University. The candidate must have experience of using one or more of these digital tools/suites: Ultra, Turnitin, Microsoft 365 and Adobe Creative Cloud applications.
This is a varied role that includes marketing, event support, social media content creation, and the development of educational resources. We therefore welcome applications from graduates who have experience or knowledge in some or all of these areas. Above all, we are looking for someone enthusiastic, willing to learn, and ready to contribute their ideas and skills to further develop the SDLA service.
Experience of using one or more of these digital tools/suites: Ultra, Turnitin, Microsoft 365, Adobe Creative Cloud applications
To think creatively and offer solutions to areas requiring improvement within the student digital experience
An interest in improving the digital skills and digital experience for students at BSU
Experience of supporting or teaching others to improve their skills
Ability to build rapport and connect with a wide range of students and staff
Experience of promoting/marketing an event, service or product
Experience of generating content for social media using Adobe or other applications
Experience of using accessibility software

At a certified Great Place to Work®, you’ll experience a progressive and nurturing environment that rewards initiative and adaptability and enjoy a career path tailored to your own aspirations.
As a Graduate Associate, you will quickly become a valued member of our agile delivery teams. Your first two years are a fast paced journey of discovery where you’ll learn what it really takes to research, design, build, test and operate world class digital services that really make a difference to people’s lives. If you want to solve real world problems for some of the biggest companies in the world, or help the government function more effectively, our Graduate Associateship is made for you.
The Graduate Associateship at Informed Solutions will equip you with the necessary skills, experience and feedback needed to take ownership of your career development and successfully make the transition from a talented graduate into an exceptional professional.
