summary_intro:
This job is for a Graduate Safety, Health, Environment, and Quality (SHEQ) Advisor . In simple terms, it’s about helping a company make sure its workplaces are safe, environmentally responsible, and delivering good-quality work.
You’ll learn from experienced professionals and build skills that are valuable in many industries whilst gaining hands-on experience on real projects.
You’ll play a meaningful role in improving safety, protecting the environment, and raising quality standards across our operations—while building a strong foundation for a long-term SHEQ career.
We value our commitment to each other, summed up in our five values, we all sign up to these: We care about safety. We lead with integrity. We strive to be better every day. We make a positive impact. We deliver to grow. We are one company united.
To be the UK's leading energy transition and utilities contractor. We are committed to leading the way in utilities and energy transition contracting; our mission is to innovate and deliver sustainability. At OCU, our passion for addressing complex challenges brings new standards of growth in our people and capabilities. OCU is an equal opportunities employer.
At OCU, we don’t just deliver infrastructure, we engineer the future. As a leader in end-to-end solutions for the utilities, digital and energy sectors, we specialise in safely and efficiently tackling complex challenges for our clients. With unrivalled expertise, industry-leading technology, and a proven track record, we’re not simply part of the market; we’re driving it forward.
Our work underpins the critical services communities across the UK rely on every day. From accelerating the transition to renewable energy to building the digital networks of tomorrow, we are committed to innovation, sustainability, and long-term impact.
When you join OCU, you’ll discover more than a career, you’ll find purpose. Here, your contribution makes a visible difference in the success of the projects you help deliver, in the growth of your colleagues, and in the positive change we create together.
We partner with some of the UK’s most recognised names in power, energy transition, water, telecoms, and digital infrastructure. As we continue to expand, we’re looking for exceptional people to grow with us.
If you’re ready to inspire, innovate and lead with purpose, we’d love to hear from you.

summary_intro:
A world where complexity is the only constant demands a new breed of company. Brave Bison is a different beast: a media, marketing and technology company purpose-built for the digital era.
Our universe is made up of award-winning business arms Brave Bison, Engage, SocialChain, and MTM. We are underpinned by leading marketing training practice, MiniMBA, as well as our very own social-first media network, delivering monthly views in the billions for some of the biggest channels in sport and entertainment across YouTube, Snap, Meta, and TikTok.
We’re a global collective who live and breathe digital, working with some of the boldest brands in the world to capitalize on the complexity that defines the modern marketing landscape.
New platforms, new behaviours, new audiences, new trends, new technologies, new regulations—our clients’ worlds get more complex daily. Their agency partnerships shouldn’t. It’s our job to cut through the chaos, make the complex simple, and navigate a clear path to growth for them.
That’s why we make it our mission to capitalize on complexity for our clients—across consultancy, capability, and execution—by crafting dynamic digital solutions that outpace tomorrow’s challenges.
We’re a proudly diverse business comprised of deep specialists across media, marketing, training, and technology. Although our skills, backgrounds, and beliefs may differ, we are united by four core shared values:
We run at change and challenge convention because we love to push the boundaries of what the world thinks is possible. We champion discovery, go deep into our clients’ worlds, and are always hungry to learn more about them, our specialisms, and each other.
We are focused in our collaboration—joining the right dots between our clients, our partners, and our herd of experts to deliver agile solutions at speed and scale. We set a shared ambition from the outset, are transparent at every stage, and always strive to make the complex simple.
We want to make working with us the best part of someone’s day. We lift one another up, find the fun in the day to day, and are committed to ensuring everyone belongs.
We believe in outcomes over outputs. We’re goal-orientated, results-driven, and data-led. We show up with passion every day. And we’re always honing our craft.
MTM is a specialist strategy and insights consultancy trusted by world-leading brands in media, entertainment, tech, and telco, including Google, Samsung, Figma, Spotify, Sony Pictures, Formula E, England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), Betway, Sky Sports, the BBC, Virgin Media O2, and Ofcom. For nearly 20 years, MTM has been powering courageous decision-making by answering our clients’ toughest questions with a blend of services across consumer, cultural, and commercial insight lenses.
London-based MTM is a three-time winner of the Market Research Society’s Agency of the Year award, as well as celebrating award wins with Adwanted including 2025 Best International Media Research Project and 2024 Research Effectiveness.
MTM is currently offering an internship within the qualitative research team. The role is a 2-3 month full-time role paid at the London Living Wage (or the Real Living Wage if based in our Leeds office).
We value candidates who are willing to get involved and work across a range of our key clients (including the BBC, YouTube, Google, Channel 4, The Football Association, etc.).
You would be helping with a range of tasks, including research, listening to interviews/focus groups, analysis, report writing, and participating in meetings.
There is also the potential opportunity for the role to become permanent if successful, joining the team as a full-time researcher following the internship.
This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is looking to develop a career in market research and, in particular, within the media and tech industry.

summary_intro:
We have a fantastic opportunity to join our Education Team in Haywards Heath office as a Trainee/Associate Client Advisor. This is the perfect role for someone with a strong educational background with ambitions to join an established, market leading insurance broker.
This role will commence in February/March 2026.
Within this role you will have the opportunity to join our exciting Education practice, where you will be supporting a team of experts on selecting and acquiring the optimum insurance programme; as well as working with a team of experienced Client Advisors and Executives on understanding our clients' business, the challenges they face, their risks, and what value looks like for them. As you progress through the training programme, you will then be in a position to learn how to advise on the best course of action for our clients risk management and work with the broking teams to manage and optimize our value proposition.
Working within an established team as part of a prominent global broker allows you to further develop your career whilst opening the door to myriad of opportunities in the future with Marsh.
Marsh Risk is a business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective.
Marsh is committed to embracing a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. We aim to attract and retain the best people and embrace diversity of age background, civil partnership status, disability, ethnic origin, family duties, gender orientation or expression, gender reassignment, marital status, nationality, parental status, personal or social status, political affiliation, race, religion and beliefs, sex/gender, sexual orientation or expression, skin color, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to providing reasonable adjustments in accordance with applicable law to any candidate with a disability to allow them to fully participate in the recruitment process.
Marsh is committed to hybrid work, which includes the flexibility of working remotely and the collaboration, connections and professional development benefits of working together in the office. All Marsh colleagues are expected to be in their local office or working onsite with clients at least three days per week. Office-based teams will identify at least one 'anchor day' per week on which their full team will be together in person.

summary_intro:
Stepping into your future - ready to learn, grow, and do meaningful work that matters. At IVC Evidensia, you’ll find a place where you can be yourself, supported by people who want to see you thrive. You’ll get hands-on experience, build your confidence, and discover just how far your passion can take you.
We are an established RCVS Accredited Equine Hospital-based just outside Lewes in the East Sussex countryside. The practice is set in the beautiful Sussex countryside at the base of the South Downs, just a few miles from the vibrant market town of Lewes and a short drive from Brighton. Direct trains to Gatwick Airport and London Victoria are available.
We have a forward-thinking and close-knit team made up of 5 Vets, 2 qualified Nurses, 2 trainee Nurses and a groom. Within the team, we have an American and RCVS Specialist in Equine Sports Medicine.
We are very well equipped with 20 inpatient stables, full surgical and hospital facilities, hospital and ambulatory diagnostic equipment, and an extensive range of treatment technology. Our in-house laboratory makes it easy for our vets to run a variety of haematological and biochemical tests on site.
Enjoy a welcoming environment with structured support and flexibility to suit your lifestyle.
You will work a 40-hour week over 5 days and be part of the out of hours rota for inpatient care.
You will be backed up by a team of experienced Vets and qualified and trainee Equine Nurses. Support and training from our resident Specialist in Equine Sports Medicine will be available and you will be assigned a VetGDP advisor and mentor for regular catch ups.
At IVC Evidensia, we’re committed to helping you shape your career your way. Our Graduate Academy offers the very best start to life in practice.
Enjoy a competitive starting salary from £36,000, alongside a range of benefits designed to help you thrive:
Joining a community where you’re seen, valued, and empowered to have an impact that’s felt. This is more than just your first step - it’s the start of something bigger.
IVC Evidensia is proud to be a Disability Confident Employer. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and are happy to discuss reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process.

summary_intro:
Are you ready to launch your career and make an impact on real-world projects from day one?
At Leonardo, we’re looking for graduates who want to be part of something bigger—shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.
We are committed to developing our graduates into leading technical or business professionals, and as such we will also support you through your preferred route for professional development. We are looking for Graduate Systems Engineer to join our team in Edinburgh.
Our Graduate Programmes give you the opportunity to work on exciting and challenging projects alongside subject matter experts.
On joining, you will receive a starting salary of £34,000 per annum, plus a £1,000 welcome bonus. You’ll also be eligible for a £1,000 exit bonus upon successful completion of the programme. In addition, you may be eligible for a Temporary Accommodation Allowance (TAA), subject to specific criteria.
We encourage you to spend at least three days each week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience.
Systems Engineers are involved in all aspects of design and development, from initial product design through to in-service support.
They look at the big picture, determine how the system needs to operate, and collaborate to produce the required overall operational behaviours. They also dive into the deepest level of detail – taking the system piece-by-piece and defining its design to the finest point. Our Systems Engineers can also actively engage in Research and Development, developing new concepts and conducting fundamental research into our future technologies.
As a Graduate Systems Engineer, you will work on real engineering problems within either the radar or the advanced targeting business area. You will have the opportunity to be involved in supporting a wide range of tasks across multiple projects/products, such as:
You will join a dynamic and innovative team who will provide day-to-day guidance and on-the-job training, introducing you to systems engineering processes, methods, technology, and tools. You will also receive targeted training, developing the engineering skills and necessary domain knowledge required to achieve technical excellence and be a successful Systems Engineer.
All of our roles require (a) a minimum of a 2:2 Bachelors/Integrated Master’s degree, or (b) a higher degree, such as a MSc or PhD in a STEM-related subject.
In addition to this, we would be interested in hearing from you if you have experience in:
This role is subject to pre-employment screening in line with the UK Government’s Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS). An additional range of Personnel Security Controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV) may apply, this could include meeting the eligibility requirements for The Security Check (SC) or Developed Vetting (DV).

We believe that a diverse workforce sparks creativity, drives innovation, and leads to better outcomes for our people, communities, and our customers. Be part of something bigger - apply now!

summary_intro:
An opportunity has arisen to recruit an Engineering Graduate (EC&I) to join the NI Engineering team in Northern Ireland and will be based at both EP Kilroot and EP Ballylumford Power Stations. The role will be site based but will include travel to other EPUKI sites or supplier locations as necessary.
The successful graduate placement will provide technical support to the Engineering team. Given the current environment in which the Ballylumford and Kilroot plant operates, the Engineering teams are supporting several key projects and outages aimed at improving the reliability, safety of operations, and addressing key technical issues that have arisen through flexible operation. The key focus of this role is to assist the site Engineers in the development and delivery of outages & critical plant improvements aimed at improving site reliability and safe operation.

This role is being advertised directly by EP UK Investments Ltd. At our discretion we will contact select recruitment partners.
We have a comprehensive Equal Opportunities Policy, which is based on equality of opportunity and the merit principle. The company is committed to appointing the best person for the job irrespective of personal factors that are not relevant to the performance of the job. In accordance with our Equal Opportunities Policy, the Company welcomes applications from all sections of the community and especially from women and the Roman Catholic Community recognising their underrepresentation in the workforce.
EPUKI is the UK division of Energetický a průmyslový holding (EPH), one of Europe’s largest private energy groups with over 70 companies and around 15,000 colleagues across the energy value chain. Operating in key European markets, EPH manages €28.9bn in assets and delivers an EBITDA of €2.6bn.
In 2025, EPH announced a major new joint venture with TotalEnergies dedicated to flexible power generation across the UK, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, and France. Once completed, this partnership will create one of Europe’s leading flexible generation platforms, strengthening energy security and supporting the continent’s transition to net zero. EPUKI’s UK and Irish flexible generation assets will form a core part of this new joint venture.
Established in 2015, EPUKI has grown rapidly through acquisitions and development, now operating a diverse portfolio of renewable and flexible power generation assets. Today, we are one of the largest independent power generators in the UK and Ireland, with revenues of c.£1.5bn and EBITDA of c.£300m. We are proud of our entrepreneurial culture and flat leadership structure, where individuals at every level can make a real impact.
Our mission is to enable the UK and Ireland’s low-carbon transition by providing reliable and flexible energy. To achieve this, we will:

Huge innovation hubs might be your kind of cosy. If you’re determined to make your mark on industry, our state-of-the-art distribution centres are the perfect environments to integrate, learn and grow alongside our amazingly supportive colleagues.

summary_intro:
Huge innovation hubs might be your kind of cosy. If you’re determined to make your mark on industry, our state-of-the-art distribution centres are the perfect environments to integrate, learn and grow alongside our amazingly supportive colleagues.
Our Supply Chain Apprenticeship is a development scheme designed to give you all the tools that you need to begin your career in the world of distribution and learn the foundations of what makes a great supply chain colleague. We are passionate about supporting your growth, that’s why internal progression has an integral part to play in all our colleagues’ development. As a Future Retail Leader the 4-year scheme will make sure you’re challenged, supported, and will give you plenty of room to grow. You will be buddied up with capable mentors, who were once in your shoes, so feel confident that you will learn from the best!
Over the 4 years, you will learn and experience every aspect of working in the operational side of Supply Chain. This may be as part of our Stoke distribution team, or our very own Home Delivery Network who deliver directly to our customers. Alongside this, you will be enrolled on to a Level 6 Supply Chain Management Degree Apprenticeship.
Dunelm is committed to becoming a fully inclusive business that is representative of our customers and locations. We recognise the value in diversity and welcome applications from all candidates regardless of sex, age, race, religion, ability, gender or sexual identity, socio-economic background or education. We are committed to making Dunelm a place where everyone can enjoy a successful career and have systems in place to support all our colleagues. We are seeking applications from candidates who share our values and celebrate diversity in all its forms.

summary_intro:
Are you ready to shape your future in accountancy and business advisory?
If you’re an enthusiastic graduate looking to join an accounting firm where you can enjoy a rewarding and progressive career, The Dains Group could offer you a range of opportunities.
Barnes Roffe are hiring for an Audit Graduate to join our Dartford office where you will have the opportunity to grow your career in auditing alongside become a qualified ACA chartered accountant.
Our audit team knows it’s all about building trust with clients. As part of our Audit team, you’ll examine company accounts, test financial systems, and ensure businesses are presenting a true and fair view of their performance. You’ll learn how to assess risk, verify transactions, and provide assurance that helps clients meet regulatory requirements and make informed decisions.
In audit you will work across a wide range of various sectors, giving you the exposure to allow you to work independently.
In June 2025, Barnes Roffe became part of The Dains Group and together, we are on course to be a Top 20 firm. The Dains Group is a fast-growing, independent accountancy practice, ranked 22nd, currently with over 1000 talented individuals across the UK and Ireland, ready to drive growth, make an impact, and offer outstanding career opportunities.
By partnering with Dains, Barnes Roffe has joined a firm with the same values and underlying service proposition that we have been delivering to our clients for over 125 years. As we are now part of a national firm, the range of specialist services we offer has widened, which in turn greatly enhances the career opportunities for our talented team.
We believe our people are our greatest asset. As one of the UK’s fastest-growing accountancy groups, we offer a dynamic, inclusive, and supportive environment where ambitious professionals can thrive.
Apply Now to join our team and start your rewarding career in auditing.

Please note that Bath Spa Graduate Scheme roles are only open to former Bath Spa students who graduated in 2025 or who will be graduating in 2026.
This information will be checked in every application. Please do not apply if you do not meet this condition, as your application will be rejected. Bath Spa have many other roles available that are open to all see the BSU job board. If you are a graduate of Bath Spa who does not meet the criteria for these roles, and would like support with your career please email gradsupportunit[at]bathspa.ac.uk
Please read the provided attachment “Bath Spa Graduate Scheme 2026 Information Sheet” for further information about the scheme'.
Please note that as of April 2024, there has been a change in the UK’s sponsorship threshold. Regrettably as the salary for this role falls beneath this, you will not be eligible for sponsorship therefore your application will automatically be rejected.
The Technical Graduate will work with Technicians and Technical Demonstrators in the Making and Construction areas (Making, Woodwork, Metalwork, Sculpture, 3D Tech and 3D Print) as necessary. The role also offers the opportunity to work with the Gallery Coordinator on exhibition installations and offsite shows. The role will support day-to-day workshop operations, maintain and tidy equipment, prepare the workshop at the start and end of the day, and assist with supporting students and staff on projects, and installation of exhibitions and open studio shows. To work with the technical team, relevant academics and the Team Leader on the development of course delivery materials including new courses, involved with H&S documentation, and to support academic staff projects requiring prototyping, material experimentation and technical problem-solving.
(This is an 18 Month Full Time Fixed Term Role)
The Technical Graduate will require skills in making and construction techniques, with a good understanding of woodwork, model-making, metalwork or other related skills, and the H&S regulations in the workshops. This would ideally suit a graduate from Product Design, Architecture, Interior Design, Fine Art, or Creative Arts Practice. They will be confident in a workshop and able to work closely with the technical team, academics, and students. They will be an ambassador for the facilities at Locksbrook, potentially supporting events that are open to members of the public (exhibitions, short courses, alumni events etc.), and assisting with the social media profile of the technical department.
For further information on the essential and desirable skills we’re looking for, please refer to the attached Job Description.

summary_intro:
To achieve our ambition, we are looking for colleagues who are ready to join us on this journey! Tomorrow can’t wait, let’s shape it together!
UK has an exciting opportunity for an Undergraduate Intern – Science Plans & Claims – Fixed-term (12 months)
We have an exciting opportunity for students who are currently undertaking a degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry (or a related subject) to join our Research & Development function, based in Southampton, on a 12-month undergraduate placement.
This placement is within our Science Plans & Claims Team and will focus on delivering science to support new product launches and answering wider scientific questions. During this placement, you will manage several key science activities and projects, to support the understanding of toxicant drivers in New Category products, as well as understanding the impact of the new innovations on wider science and tobacco harm reduction questions. You will also be responsible for scoping and defining scientific studies, conducting/supporting testing, analysing data and producing insights with respect to these scientific questions.
We make significant investments in Research and Development to deliver innovations that satisfy or anticipate consumer needs and generate growth for the business. We conduct cutting-edge research to evaluate our Potentially Reduced Risk Products (PRRPs) and apply the highest standards for product safety and quality. Successful applicants will be involved in our extensive scientific research program which spans a broad spectrum of scientific fields - including molecular biology, human biology, toxicology, chemistry, biomedical sciences, psychology, neuroscience, sensorial science, data science, computer science, product design, and engineering disciplines.
In the UK, we offer 12-months placement opportunities (starting on 1st September 2026) to undergraduate students looking to gain practical experience within a vibrant and innovative industrial setting. As part of the scheme, you will be partnered with a mentor, have regular reviews with your Line Manager and work on projects that impact the business.
BAT has an established placement programme, with a dedicated Placement Team, which provides training and development throughout the placement. This includes sessions for onboarding, presentation skills, critical thinking, scientific poster presentations and ‘speed networking’ with senior management. Successful applicants are provided with multiple opportunities to develop transferable skills in addition to gaining ‘hands on’ experience in a technical discipline.
As part of the scheme students get a chance to cultivate their independent thinking and problem-solving skills in addition to working in and contributing to a team. Cross functional/department working and participation in other research activities is also encouraged, where appropriate. Previous work experience in a practical ‘hands-on’ role would be useful but not essential.
This role is due to start in September 2026, and we will be shortlisting applications and carrying out video/online interviews whilst the advert is live. We will look to make an offer to the successful candidate as close to the closing date as possible. However, the vetting and onboarding processes for successful candidates won’t begin until the role is opened in our system, which is likely to be later in 2026, so we will contact successful candidates again to commence these processes when the position opens.

We have an exciting opportunity for students who are currently undertaking a degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry (or a related subject) to join our Research & Development function, based in Southampton, on a 12-month undergraduate placement.
This placement is within our Science Plans & Claims Team and will focus on delivering science to support new product launches and answering wider scientific questions. During this placement, you will manage several key science activities and projects, to support the understanding of toxicant drivers in New Category products, as well as understanding the impact of the new innovations on wider science and tobacco harm reduction questions. You will also be responsible for scoping and defining scientific studies, conducting/supporting testing, analysing data and producing insights with respect to these scientific questions.
We make significant investments in Research and Development to deliver innovations that satisfy or anticipate consumer needs and generate growth for the business. We conduct cutting-edge research to evaluate our Potentially Reduced Risk Products (PRRPs) and apply the highest standards for product safety and quality. Successful applicants will be involved in our extensive scientific research program which spans a broad spectrum of scientific fields - including molecular biology, human biology, toxicology, chemistry, biomedical sciences, psychology, neuroscience, sensorial science, data science, computer science, product design, and engineering disciplines.
In the UK, we offer 12-months placement opportunities (starting on 1st September 2026) to undergraduate students looking to gain practical experience within a vibrant and innovative industrial setting. As part of the scheme, you will be partnered with a mentor, have regular reviews with your Line Manager and work on projects that impact the business.
BAT has an established placement programme, with a dedicated Placement Team, which provides training and development throughout the placement. This includes sessions for onboarding, presentation skills, critical thinking, scientific poster presentations and ‘speed networking’ with senior management. Successful applicants are provided with multiple opportunities to develop transferable skills in addition to gaining ‘hands on’ experience in a technical discipline.
As part of the scheme students get a chance to cultivate their independent thinking and problem-solving skills in addition to working in and contributing to a team. Cross functional/department working and participation in other research activities is also encouraged, where appropriate. Previous work experience in a practical ‘hands-on’ role would be useful but not essential.
This role is due to start in September 2026, and we will be shortlisting applications and carrying out video/online interviews whilst the advert is live. We will look to make an offer to the successful candidate as close to the closing date as possible. However, the vetting and onboarding processes for successful candidates won’t begin until the role is opened in our system, which is likely to be later in 2026, so we will contact successful candidates again to commence these processes when the position opens.
We’re one of the few companies named as a Global Top Employer by the Top Employers Institute – certified in offering excellent employee conditions.
At BAT, we champion collaboration, inclusion, and partnership as the bedrock of our values. We wish to foster an environment where every individual can thrive, irrespective of factors such as gender, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, skills, experience, education, socio-economic and professional background, as well as diverse perspectives and thinking styles. We recognise that our strength lies in embracing talent from all walks of life, empowering us to develop our culture of inclusivity and better achieve our business objectives.
We view career breaks not as obstacles but as opportunities and encourage everyone, without hesitation, to apply. Through our Global Returners program, we provide support to professionals seeking to re-enter the workforce after an extended absence, be it for family care, parental leave, national service, sabbatical, or starting their own venture.
Come bring your difference and see what is possible for you at BAT. Learn more about our culture and our award winning employee experience here.
We take pride in being a Disability Confident Employer. If you need any reasonable adjustments or accommodations to be made during the recruitment process to support you performing at your best, please inform the recruitment partner who will be in touch should your profile be selected for the role you applied for. We are wholeheartedly committed to optimising your prospects of success by making suitable arrangements so that you may showcase your full potential.

Conduct open-source due diligence research across multiple jurisdictions, analysing a wide range of sources to identify potential compliance risks.
Prepare clear and concise reports summarising findings related to corruption, political exposure, sanctions, and other integrity concerns.
Work on diverse cases, shifting between different topics and geographies—for example, assessing a complex legal dispute in the US before analysing an offshore corporate structure in another jurisdiction.
Progress over time into region-specific research aligned with your language skills and regional expertise.
Navigate complex, cross-border risk landscapes and apply sound judgement when evaluating sources and information.
Collaborate with senior staff on more complex projects as you develop.
Build subject-matter expertise in regional regulatory and compliance risks.
Contribute to training new team members once fully onboarded.
Support business development activities where needed.
Training: We pride ourselves on producing market-leading work. To maintain these high standards, we provide comprehensive one-to-one training. New analysts work closely with an experienced researcher over the first 4-6 months of their career to bring them up to speed and equip them with all the skills necessary to become an expert in due diligence and compliance. From then on, all senior staff actively work with new joiners to ensure that they hit the ground running, and continue to mentor analysts over the course of their career at Anthesis.
Career development: Having mastered our core entry level product, analysts are exposed to a range of career paths. As a fast-expanding company, we ensure that employees are given all the tools to develop professionally – whether it’s in-depth research, business development, client exposure or management. We build our company from the ground up, and many of our most senior staff started with us as analysts.
Company culture: Anthesis is a dynamic company with a friendly, young and energetic team that support each other on work. All members of our team work together to create an environment in which our staff are able to reach their potential. We offer competitive pay, clear career progression, and visa sponsorship to those that need it.
Strong professional work ethic, with a self-starter attitude and a commitment to taking ownership of personal learning and development.
Basic understanding of, and interest in, due diligence and compliance risks; experience within a commercial research environment is highly desirable.
Fluent written and verbal English, suitable for use in a commercial context.
Excellent research and writing abilities, including strong attention to detail and the capacity to identify, interpret, and summarise information from diverse sources under time pressure.
Strong time-management skills, with the ability to handle multiple concurrent projects and meet tight deadlines.
Fluency in at least one foreign language. Languages of particular interest include Arabic, Mandarin, Portuguese, Spanish, German, Italian, Greek and French, though applicants with other language skills are also encouraged to apply.
Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline from an accredited university.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
Demonstrated interest in international affairs and global business.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
Receptiveness to feedback and willingness to learn and develop.
Work within a highly motivated team in an innovative and rapidly growing global company.
Opportunity to have a direct impact and be a key part of the growth and development of the business and the team.
Exposure to a wide range of clients and projects on a global basis.
Competitive salary in line with experience and skills.
Competitive benefits including flexible working, 25 days holiday and two volunteering days off and the day off for your Birthday!

summary_intro:
Transactions: Business Intelligence
Wallbrook (part of Anthesis Group) is seeking highly motivated graduates to join our team of investigative due diligence researchers. The successful candidates will have completed (or will be studying towards) a qualitative research degree – in history, politics, languages or other similar fields – and be fluent in at least one foreign language.
We are interested in candidates with fluency in a variety of languages, particularly Arabic, Mandarin, Portuguese, Spanish, German, Italian, Greek and French. We also welcome applications from candidates with more niche languages.
The due diligence team at Anthesis Group provides leading global intelligence and compliance risk services, and specialises in enhanced due diligence investigations. Our team’s regional and sectoral expertise help the world’s foremost organisations make informed, ethical decisions about the professionals and businesses they work with, the assets they acquire, and where and how they operate.
As an Analyst in our Due Diligence team, you will begin your career specialising in open-source investigative research. You will contribute to the production of due diligence reports that identify major compliance red flags associated with companies or individuals, including corruption risks, political exposure, sanctions, and other integrity-related issues.
Anthesis Group is a global sustainability and ESG company. We provide a wide suite of sustainability solutions to clients across the world. Anthesis is a certified B-Corp – reflecting the company’s commitment to sustainability and employee-friendly policies – and the company has an employee shareholder scheme, allowing Anthesis employees to share in the company’s success.
Once fully trained, analysts will expand the scope of their work – taking on more complicated projects in conjunction with senior staff; developing regional expertise in regulatory and compliance risks; training new members of staff; and taking on business development responsibilities. For exceptional candidates, our analyst role lays the foundations for career progression at Anthesis.
We ask candidates to submit their CV and a cover letter, outlining what attracts them to due diligence and Wallbrook. Please note that applications without a cover letter will not be considered. If you require any reasonable adjustments to be made to your application process or need this job advert in a different format, just let us know and we will be happy to help.

summary_intro:
At Alexander Dennis, our vision is to lead the evolution of sustainable on-road mass transportation and mobility.
We design, deliver, and support market-leading buses and coaches that help reduce emissions, improve air quality, and keep communities connected. Every role contributes to that mission whether you're engineering, driving sales, improving production, or supporting our customers.
You’ll play a key role in supporting our Aftermarket Finance team, working closely with the Finance Controller - Parts, as well as the wider central finance function. In this role, you’ll take ownership of forecasting activities, financial analysis, and balance sheet reconciliations, while ensuring compliance with ICFR. You’ll develop strong relationships across the business, providing insightful reporting and supporting both operational and finance teams to drive effective decision-making.
You’ll bring strong analytical capability, confidence working with data, and excellent communication skills. You should be comfortable working proactively and independently, partnering with stakeholders both inside and outside of finance. Advanced Excel skills and experience with financial systems will help you succeed in this role.
Because we know that to deliver on our vision, people have to feel supported and inspired:
Be part of something that’s changing cities, improving air quality, helping public transport evolve.
Training programmes, mentorship, opportunities to take on new roles, broaden skills.
An inclusive environment; your voice matters; we treat people fairly.

requirement_summery:
Work under the guidance of senior engineers to produce detailed high voltage substation design packages, compliant to required client and national technical standards (ENA/BS/IEC/IEEE), including preparing calculations and technical/equipment specification documentation.
Participate in FEED stage projects, including production of technical reports and presentations.
Support the preparation of technical solutions for project proposals.
Work independently or as part of a project team and manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
Support 'Safety by Design' approach on all projects, at all times.
Maintain compliance to CDM Regulations and all other legal and regulatory requirements associated with the nature of cable and electrical system design.
Understand wider industry best practices and client technical standards/procedures for construction, operations & maintenance, and decommissioning, in order to drive safety, constructability, and operability throughout whole asset lifecycles.
Maintain project compliance to Burns & McDonnell’s UK Integrated Management System.
Always strive to offer world-class customer service, to drive client success.
Be an ambassador for Burns & McDonnell at all times through acting in accordance with expected high ethical and moral standards, and in adherence to Burns & McDonnell Code of Conduct.
Demonstrate creativity, foresight, and judgment in anticipating and solving problems.
Technical development of knowledge and skills through a combination of training courses, project experience, mentoring, and self-teaching.
Personal professional development and partaking in professional bodies and industry groups.
Undertake other duties and responsibilities as may reasonably be asked of this position by management.
Bachelor's degree in a Civil/Structural engineering discipline, from an accredited institution is required.
Membership of a relevant professional Engineering Institution (ICE, IStructE, etc.) is preferred.
IT literate, with good knowledge of using Microsoft Office applications.
Knowledge of using CAD software (e.g. AutoCAD) for engineering design.
Excellent written & verbal communication skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to apply diversified knowledge of principles and practices to a range of assignments.
Able to manage tasks on multiple projects and conflicting deadlines.
Able to work autonomously and/or as part of a project team.
Pro-active in building knowledge and understanding of the civil engineering profession and electricity transmission & distribution industry.
Engaged in the engineering community and how we can drive success for our clients.
Ability to maintain focus on technical work to meet deadlines.
Attention to detail in production of design drawings and technical documentation.
Ability to develop innovative and practical solutions to a range of problems, and an understanding of how one issue may be part of a much larger solution.
Ability to make an effective and collaborative contribution to the team through sharing knowledge, promoting ideas, and valuing the contribution of all team members.
Driven to provide outstanding customer service.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Strong attention to detail, facilitation, team building, collaboration, organization, and problem-solving skills.

Engineers in Training-EIT Certification preferred.

Rooted in our transformative power, it communicates our work in tackling inequalities, removing barriers, and improving the life chances of the people and communities we serve.
We nurture our very special culture. summary_intro:
We are the independent expert in assurance and risk management. Driven by our purpose, to safeguard life, property, and the environment, we empower our customers and their stakeholders with facts and reliable insights so that critical decisions can be made with confidence.
As a trusted voice for many of the world's most successful organizations, we use our knowledge to advance safety and performance, set industry benchmarks, and inspire and invent solutions to tackle global transformations.
We help customers navigate the complex transition to a decarbonized and more sustainable energy future. We do this by assuring that energy systems work safely and effectively, using solutions that are increasingly digital. We also help industries and governments to navigate the many complex, interrelated transitions taking place globally and regionally, in the energy industry.
Join DNV’s Jack-up Engineering team and work on some of the most complex offshore energy projects in the world. Make a difference and contribute to engineering assessments supporting the installation of offshore wind farms and the safe operation of offshore vessels globally. Here at DNV, what we do matters. Whether it’s helping the Energy Industry transition to a more decarbonized and sustainable future or helping protect life, property and the environment, every day, what you do, will make a difference. This is our shared purpose and one that our people are proud to be part of.
Our specialist Jack-up Engineering Service is part of the wider Offshore Infrastructures department here at DNV. The work we do is at the forefront of implementing the green energy transition around the world today, with a focus on the installation and operation of jack-up vessels. Our team provides sophisticated solutions and engineering assessments to support offshore renewable energy installation projects around the globe, as well as ensuring safe operations for our oil and gas customers. Our work involves solving complex engineering challenges associated with the installation and operation of jack-up vessels used in offshore wind and oil and gas projects.
As part of the team, you will support the delivery of engineering analyses and technical assessments for clients operating around the world, gaining practical experience while contributing to the safe and efficient installation of offshore energy infrastructure.
Our Jack-up Engineering team is a diverse group of structural, mechanical, and geotechnical engineers specializing in the installation and operation of jack-up vessels used in offshore wind turbine installation and oil and gas activities. Our projects are located across the globe, from Alaska to New Zealand, providing genuine variety in the technical challenges you will encounter. You will contribute to engineering assessments and analyses supporting offshore energy developments in a wide range of environments and operating conditions.
While our projects are global, this role is primarily based in our Central London office (a short walk from Waterloo and Blackfriars). Being in the office regularly at the start will help you get fully immersed in our structural and geotechnical teams and build strong connections across DNV’s offshore engineering community. Once you’re settled into the role and up to speed, we offer flexible hybrid working—typically a 3/2 split between office and home—to give you the best balance of collaboration and autonomy.
From day one, you will be supported with a structured development plan to help you grow professionally. Working alongside experienced engineers and technical experts, you will contribute to high-impact projects while developing your technical, commercial, and project management skills.

We appreciate that applying for a Graduate opportunity, for some, can be a new or daunting experience, which is why we try to make our process as simple, transparent, and as engaging as possible.
Our application deadline is Sunday 12th April 2026 and we anticipate that our Assessment Centre will take place on Tuesday 12th May 2026.

Support scope preparation and execution during planned and unplanned outages.
Deliver EC&I improvement projects inside and outside of planned outages.
Responsibility for the management and delivery of individual work packages within and outside of the outage.
Develop a criticality matrix, scoring all EPNI DCS, Protection, Electrical systems.
Review spares holding for key electrical and control systems taking into account obsolescence and product lifecycles.
Assist with compliance against statutory requirements (e.g., DSEAR, minimum engineering standards, Management of Change, etc.).
Major capital project development and delivery.
Engineering and Production team activities on a large Combined Cycle Gas Fired Power Station.
Understanding of the commercial drivers and statutory compliance requirements impacting large scale thermal generation plants.
Working as part of a multi-disciplinary engineering team.
Appreciation and interpretation of logic within plant Distributed Control System
Plant maintenance and RCM techniques/principles.
Exposure to senior management through the provision of project status briefings.
Operational data analysis.
Exposure to complex Electrical and control issues, fault-finding, and problem-solving
Working with contractors.
Technical Incident Investigations, Root Cause Analysis, and Process Safety.
Build a portfolio of evidence and skills for working towards Chartered Status.
Experience of power plant or similar industrial experience (desirable).

summary_intro:
Big enough to matter. Personal enough to care. That’s BDO.
Ready for a year of learning that goes beyond the classroom? Kick-start a meaningful, impactful career with a year-long BDO Industrial Placement – which could even lead to a graduate role offer.
The programme starts on Monday, 21st September 2026 for a firm-wide induction (you need to be able to attend).
You’ll work with real responsibility and purpose, across a variety of companies, clients, and projects. Surrounded by talented, passionate people, you’ll explore your strengths, discover what excites you, and build skills that matter. All in a team that’s invested in helping you succeed.
In Audit, you’ll work on varied, challenging projects across multiple sectors as part of a high-performing team. You’ll gain hands-on experience in assessing financial statements, understanding businesses inside and out, and providing valuable insights that make a real difference to our clients.
You’re curious, resilient and adaptable. You think logically, enjoy problem-solving, and want to make a difference. You bring energy and a willingness to learn – we’ll support you to build the rest. We’re also big on collaboration, so we’ll help you grow your communication and relationship-building skills. And we’ll expect you to be committed to making the most of every opportunity.
One thing to note: you’ll need to live within a commutable distance of the office you apply to. Relocation support is not provided, so please consider this carefully before applying. Time in the office matters; for your learning, for building relationships, and for being part of our culture.
To be a second-year student on a four-year undergraduate degree, seeking a third-year work placement
On track for a minimum 2:2 degree in any discipline
Three A-levels or equivalent at grades A*-C (excluding General Studies and Extended Projects) or four Scottish Advanced Highers at grade A-B. Please note we do not use UCAS points. You'll be asked to provide evidence if you're successful in securing a placement with us
GCSEs at grade 4 and above in Maths and English, or Scottish National 5 grade A-C. You’ll also need to provide evidence if successful
The right to work in the UK from the start date
We want you to know what to expect, so here’s the typical process:
Online assessments (with the option to sit these in our office, where we can provide a laptop and space if you don’t have access to one).
Virtual assessment centre and interview.
We’ll keep you updated at each stage and share tips to help you prepare. And just so you know: we don’t use AI in any part of our candidate screening process. Every application is reviewed by a real person.
We’ve got 18 offices across the UK, but wherever you join us, you’ll be part of a team that cares. You’ll learn by doing, be supported by people who’ve been in your shoes, and build skills that actually matter. We’re serious about your well-being, adaptable about how you work, and offer benefits that support you inside and outside of work.
Big enough to open doors. Personal enough to walk through them with you.
Go Beyond the Ordinary with BDO.
Our firm is distinctive because we preserve and build on the strengths of our culture and the characteristics that make us successful and different. We look for people from all kinds of backgrounds who share these same qualities.

It’s a great place to learn, with a strong team and a diverse portfolio of Landscape Architecture projects to practice and hone your skills and support you through Chartership. We operate as integrated designers alongside our colleagues in other disciplines such as Transportation and Water Environment and as a standalone service.
Our philosophy is simple: we invest in our people and build partnerships with our stakeholders, resulting in a dynamic and successful business that benefits everyone. As a multidisciplinary environmental and engineering consultancy, our outputs contribute to the built environment we all occupy. Our four values include ‘living our best life’ and ‘celebrating our team’, and we provide loads of opportunities to do just that. Recent external recognition for this includes Gold Investors in People ‘We Invest in Wellbeing’ Accreditation and ‘Best Place to Work’ Winners, SoGlos Gloucestershire Business Awards.
We currently number 90 people, based out of four principal offices, and celebrated our 10-year anniversary in 2025!
We believe in having equity throughout our business and welcome applications from people from all backgrounds. We know that diverse teams are strong teams and strive to be a great home for all our people. Let us know what you need to be your best self with Rappor.
We will acknowledge your application immediately and will be reviewing applications for this position on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible and applications will close no later than 12 April 2026. Our selection process will include written questions as a qualifier for in person assessment in our Cheltenham office. The start date for the position will be as early as your circumstances allow and in September 2026 at the latest.

It is a two to three year programme in which you will study with the University of Law, the UK's largest legal training provider, to prepare for the Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE).
The programme combines full-time legal work (five days a week) with a dedicated study day to ensure you are fully prepared for the SQE assessments.
Upon passing SQE1 and SQE2, and subject to a character and suitability assessment, you can apply for admission as a solicitor.
Graduates with a qualifying law degree.
This apprenticeship programme is only open to candidates who will be under the age of 22 on the programme enrolment date.
Applications close: Friday 10th April 2026 (we may close earlier depending on application volume).
Application review: Applications will be reviewed and candidates will be contacted with the outcome.
Professional Skill Assessment: Shortlisted candidates will be sent an assessment to be completed and returned.
Informal call: Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a brief introductory call.
Assessment Days: Candidates who are successful at all stages will be invited to attend on one of the following dates: Monday 11th May or Tuesday 12th May in our Southport office.
Following the assessment day, successful candidates will be invited to attend a final interview and presentation, which will take place during the week commencing 18th May to 5th June.
35 hours working week
Bonus scheme (subject to targets being met)
35 days holiday a year including bank holidays and Christmas Closure, with an option to purchase up to 3 extra days holiday per year, until you long service award the 3 days after your 5th, 7th, and 9th full year of employment
Pension scheme with tax-efficient salary sacrifice option
Life Assurance Policy
Medicash policy to cover some dental, optical and other medical expenses
Company sick pay
Enhanced Maternity, Paternity and IVF schemes
Flexible, agile working environment with a positive work-life balance
Varied calendar of funded company social events
Monthly voucher awards for winning nominees
A genuinely supportive and friendly culture

summary_intro:
Manchester, Liverpool, Leeds, Southport and Birmingham
With the flexibility to work from home and collaborate in-office when needed. We believe we offer our colleagues the best hybrid and flexible working practices, balancing working from home with time collaborating and socialising with colleagues in our modern office.
Fletchers Solicitors have a fantastic opportunity to join our growing team as a Graduate Solicitor Apprentice. As an apprentice, you will begin a structured 23-year pathway toward qualification as a solicitor while gaining hands-on experience within a dynamic legal environment. You will work alongside experienced legal professionals, supporting a range of legal matters including research, drafting documents, preparing case files, and assisting with client communications. Throughout the programme, you will combine practical, on-the-job training with formal study, developing strong legal knowledge, analytical skills, and professional judgement. This role offers an excellent opportunity to build a long-term legal career while contributing meaningfully to the team and delivering high-quality support to clients.
As an apprentice, you will gain comprehensive experience in the field of clinical negligence, working on a broad and varied caseload of claims arising from medical errors. You will be involved in matters ranging from cosmetic and dental treatment issues to more complex and high-value cases, including catastrophic injuries, birth injuries, and delayed cancer diagnoses. This position offers the opportunity to develop a strong understanding of the legal and medical aspects of clinical negligence, as you support clients through often sensitive and challenging circumstances. You will also build practical skills in case management, investigation, and client communication, while gaining exposure to both straightforward claims and highly complex litigation.
Further details about each stage of the process will be provided to candidates as they progress.
We reserve the right to close this role before the date specified depending on the calibre and volume of candidates.
Fletchers is a fast-growing, dynamic law firm specialising in personal injury and clinical negligence law, with outstanding rankings in both The Legal 500 and Chambers & Partners . Following several strategic acquisitions, we have evolved into the Fletchers Group, with ambitious plans for continued growth and innovation. We aspire to be the best place to work in the legal sector. Our workplace culture is inclusive, informal, and supportive, with a strong focus on colleague wellbeing and happiness. We are proud to offer some of the best hybrid and flexible working arrangements in the industry because we understand that balance drives performance. At Fletchers, we also value connection and collaboration. We create exciting opportunities for teams to come together and thrive. Whether you're starting your career or aiming for leadership, you'll find a clear path to progress and development, from apprenticeships and professional qualifications to senior roles and Partnership. We seek out a broad range of challenging, high-quality legal work, enabling our people to build meaningful and progressive careers. And we don't just talk about development – we invest in it, with a significant proportion of our colleagues working towards relevant qualifications at any given time. We reward those who help build our success and live our values. Our benefits package is designed to grow with you, offering real opportunities to share in our long-term strength. Our base pay and bonus structure is built to recognise and reward high performance. Join us and be part of a law firm that's not only growing but redefining what it means to work in legal services.
Fletchers Group is an inclusive employer with a diverse workforce: we welcome applications from any and all backgrounds. We're committed to providing a culture and environment where everyone can thrive, understanding and celebrating that no colleague is the same. We're proud of our work on the Disability Confident scheme, signed up to BITC's Race at Work charter, and working towards Henpicked's Menopause and Menstrual Friendly accreditations.
summary_bullets:
It is a two to three year programme in which you will study with the University of Law, the UK's largest legal training provider, to prepare for the Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE).
The programme combines full-time legal work (five days a week) with a dedicated study day to ensure you are fully prepared for the SQE assessments.
Upon passing SQE1 and SQE2, and subject to a character and suitability assessment, you can apply for admission as a solicitor.
Graduates with a qualifying law degree.
This apprenticeship programme is only open to candidates who will be under the age of 22 on the programme enrolment date.
Applications close: Friday 10th April 2026 (we may close earlier depending on application volume).
Application review: Applications will be reviewed and candidates will be contacted with the outcome.
Professional Skill Assessment: Shortlisted candidates will be sent an assessment to be completed and returned.
Informal call: Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a brief introductory call.
Assessment Days: Candidates who are successful at all stages will be invited to attend on one of the following dates: Monday 11th May or Tuesday 12th May in our Southport office.
Following the assessment day, successful candidates will be invited to attend a final interview and presentation, which will take place during the week commencing 18th May to 5th June.
35 hours working week
Bonus scheme (subject to targets being met)
35 days holiday a year including bank holidays and Christmas Closure, with an option to purchase up to 3 extra days holiday per year, until you long service award the 3 days after your 5th, 7th, and 9th full year of employment
Pension scheme with tax-efficient salary sacrifice option
Life Assurance Policy
Medicash policy to cover some dental, optical and other medical expenses
Company sick pay
Enhanced Maternity, Paternity and IVF schemes
Flexible, agile working environment with a positive work-life balance
Varied calendar of funded company social events
Monthly voucher awards for winning nominees
A genuinely supportive and friendly culture
Ongoing training and professional development opportunities
Balancing study and work commitments: balancing one study day per week, successfully managing academic requirements alongside your job responsibilities, ensuring both study and work targets are met.
Speaking with our clients face to face, or by telephone and corresponding with them by email, letter, or case management app, always in a professional and courteous way
Obtaining and drafting a full and accurate timeline of events based on the clients' instructions
Acting on instructions promptly, whether from clients or from training principals and supervising team members
Developing and maintaining knowledge of claims processes and best practices
Ensuring accurate information is taken and recorded onto the case management system
Monitoring and managing a task list efficiently to ensure cases are progressed appropriately
Ensure individual targets/KPIs are met
Keeping clients informed of progress
Action correspondence on files and deal with accordingly
Assisting others with any other reasonable duties as and when required
Liaising with and taking instruction from supervisors
Adhering to data protection/GDPR & Fletchers office processes
Any other reasonable duties
Grade A-C in GCSE English language and Mathematics
LLB-2.2 or above

summary_intro:
Internship opportunities for 2026-27
Are you a young Christian who is passionate about issues of justice and peace? Do you want to explore the intersection of faith, policy, and politics, and potentially pursue a career in one of these fields? The Joint Public Issues Team (JPIT) is recruiting to two full-time paid internship positions to start in September 2026.
Interns work as part of a small ecumenical team on a diverse range of tasks and initiatives including communications, policy, campaigning, and supporter engagement, contributing to the public advocacy and political engagement work of the Baptist, Methodist, and United Reformed Churches.
JPIT is a partnership between the Baptist Union of Great Britain, the Methodist Church, the United Reformed Church, and the Church of Scotland is an associate partner. Its purpose is to help the Churches work together for peace and justice through listening, learning, praying, speaking, and acting on public policy issues. It is a team that brings together around ten staff working across the denominations. In recent years it has focused on issues around poverty, the economy, refugees and migration, the environment, peace and conflict, and politics.
These internships provide opportunities to develop skills in campaigning, communications, research, and policy within a dynamic team environment. There will be opportunities for professional and personal learning and development to equip the intern for further employment after their time on the internship. Whilst we are looking for some evidence of certain skills and experience, candidates will have the opportunity to develop relevant skills during their time in the role.
They are full-time paid roles with fixed-term contracts to the end of August 2027, and a salary of £26,936.00 per year (we are committed to paying at least the London Living Wage). The roles are based in the Methodist Connexional Team which offers hybrid working arrangements, with an expectation of spending at least two days a week at an office base in central London.
Applications from a diverse range of people. You should be aged 21-30, have excellent communication skills, be enthusiastic and willing to take on new challenges, be interested in political engagement and be a practicing Christian. An Enhanced DBS Check will be required.
Thank you for considering joining our inclusive and welcoming team that strives for excellence and values employee wellbeing.
We value and support all those who join our team through a positive work-life balance augmented by generous annual leave (plus an extra 3 days over Christmas/New Year), TOIL, flexi-leave and an on-site Well-being Adviser service. We offer a generous occupational pension scheme, where the Methodist Church will pay double the employee contribution up to a maximum of 16% employer contribution.
The Methodist Church is an inclusive and supportive employer. We are actively committed to encouraging applications from people of all backgrounds. We welcome applications from people of Black, Asian, and other Minority Ethnic groups.
We are a Disability Confident employer and welcome applications from people living with disabilities. If you need any reasonable adjustments at any stage, please reach out to us.
This post is restricted to Christians due to the nature of the role. The Occupational Requirement section under Schedule 9 (Part 1) of the Equality Act 2010 applies.

summary_intro:
At Costain, we help to improve people's lives by creating connected, sustainable infrastructure that enables people and the planet to thrive. We work together to shape, create, and deliver pioneering solutions that transform the performance of the UK's infrastructure ecosystem across energy, water, transportation and defence markets. Through our collaboration with customers, partners, communities, and wider industry, we will deliver an infrastructure fit for a better future.
Our programme focuses on helping individuals to learn a mix of both Leadership and Technical skills. We offer a structured training programme to enable graduates to work towards achieving Chartership in their chosen field. Graduates may have the opportunity, after the first 8 - 10 months, to rotate and work on a number of exciting and progressive projects around the UK during the 2-year period, experiencing the best we have to offer across the different sectors we work in. Our line managers are fully supportive of the Graduate Development Programme and will be involved in helping you along the way.
The purpose of the role is to develop the skills required to become responsible for key elements of work on a project, taking a significant role in mechanical engineering and technical delivery, as well as managing aspects of time, cost, and quality. You will acquire technical, leadership, and project management skills and experience.
You will have achieved or are on track to have achieved a Bachelor's degree at grade 2:2 or above in a related engineering degree subject. Excellent organisation and time management skills. Possess a willingness to learn and take on new challenges. Have a passion for Costain's Carbon Net Zero targets. Excellent communication and presentation skills, verbal and written. Appreciate project time pressures. Ability to work both independently and cooperatively in a fast-paced environment. Please note that if you are invited to interview, we will require you to produce your passport and/or right to work documentation. As some of our project sites are based in remote locations, it is worth noting that you will be required to have the ability to travel to the site.
Costain helps to improve people's lives with integrated, leading-edge, smart infrastructure solutions across the UK’s energy, water, transportation, and defence markets. We help our clients improve their business performance by increasing capacity, improving customer service, safeguarding security, enhancing resilience, decarbonising, and delivering increased efficiency. Our vision is to be the UK's leading smart infrastructure solutions company. We will achieve this by focusing on blue-chip clients whose major spending plans are underpinned by strategic national needs, regulatory commitments, legislation, or essential performance requirements. We offer our clients leading-edge solutions that are digitally optimised through future-shaping strategic consultancy, consultancy and advisory, digital technology solutions, asset optimisation, and complex programme delivery. Our culture and values underpin everything we do.
Costain appreciates the time and effort taken when applying for one of our positions but, due to the high volume of responses, we are unable to provide individual feedback on candidates at the application phase. We do share feedback following an interview. A Disability Confident employer will generally offer an interview to any applicant that discloses they have a disability and meets the minimum criteria for the job as defined by the employer. It is important to note that in certain recruitment situations such as high-volume, seasonal, and high-peak times, the employer may wish to limit the overall numbers of interviews offered to both disabled and non-disabled people.

Whether you're just starting your career or looking to build on your early experience, you'll find a team of dedicated professionals here who are passionate about delivering high-quality services and who genuinely invest in their colleagues' growth.
Celnor Group is a UK-based environmental services group operating across the Testing, Inspection, Certification and Compliance (TICC) landscape. With a growing portfolio of specialist businesses, Celnor provides essential services that protect people, property and the environment. While each business retains its own identity, culture and technical specialism, all are supported by a central group function that invests in people, systems and long-term sustainable growth.
We are looking for a motivated Graduate Geotechnical Engineer to join our team based in Falkirk. This is a fantastic opportunity to launch your career in geotechnical and environmental site investigation, gaining hands-on site experience from day one.
Working primarily in the field, you will support experienced engineers across a variety of site investigation and geotechnical projects, developing your technical skills in a supportive, collaborative environment. You will be mentored and guided as you build towards professional accreditation.
We're looking for someone who is eager to get stuck in and grow their career in a hands-on environment. You don't need years of experience, we'll provide the training, mentorship, and support to help you develop. What matters most is a genuine interest in geotechnical engineering, a practical mindset, and the drive to deliver quality work.
You'll be joining a business where your contribution matters from day one and where professionalism, integrity, and teamwork are genuinely valued. With exciting projects across Scotland and the North of England, Aitken Laboratories is a great place to start and build your career. As part of the wider Celnor Group, you'll also benefit from group-wide investment, shared expertise, and long-term career development opportunities as the organisation continues to grow.
We offer a competitive starting salary of £26,000 - £29,000 per annum and provide a comprehensive range of benefits including:
Aitken Laboratories is an equal opportunities employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace.
Celnor Group and its businesses manage recruitment directly. We do not require agency support for this role and will only engage with recruitment partners from our preferred supplier list where necessary.

summary_intro:
London College of Contemporary Arts (LCCA) delivers creative and industry-focused higher education to a diverse student community across fashion, design, business, hospitality, and games. Our students are ambitious and practical, many entering industries where access to networks and real-world experience makes the difference between graduating and actually working in the sector.
We are looking for an Employer Engagement and Placements Consultant to build and manage a strong network of industry opportunities across Fashion, Graphic Design, and Games, with a particular focus on Fashion placements. This is an externally facing role centered on relationship building, not teaching. You will work closely with our Careers Consultants to introduce employers to student talent and help students access real-world experience.
You will not be expected to deliver lectures or formal teaching. The role is about brokering opportunities and building trusted industry relationships.
This is a flexible, part-time position of approximately two days per week. The role is largely remote, with occasional visits to our London campus (typically one or two days per month and during key placement periods). We are open to flexible working patterns and this role may suit someone combining consultancy, freelance, or industry work alongside a higher education role.
We are interested in candidates with strong professional credibility and networks within the creative industries. You may currently work in:
Experience in higher education is welcome but not essential.
This role offers the opportunity to shape how creative students access industry and to build a genuine bridge between education and the professional world. You will have autonomy, flexibility, and the ability to work remotely, while being part of a collaborative Careers and Employability team.
Please note: Candidates must have the right to work in the UK. Only applicants shortlisted for an interview will be contacted. We do not offer visa sponsorships.
We are committed to ensuring our workforce is reflective of our diverse student population, striving to increase the representation of age, disability, gender identity and expression, religion, race, sex, sexual orientation, and socio-economic background of our employees.
We’re also committed to providing adjustments to those who may require support with the recruitment process.

Kick-start your career at the heart of a global technology leader. We’re looking for a motivated, analytical recent graduate to join our UK Commercial team in a pivotal strategic role. This opportunity offers direct exposure to senior leaders and the chance to work closely with teams across Sales, Vendor Management, Finance, and Marketing. If you're a recent graduate looking to begin your career in a fast-moving, growth-focused environment where you can influence decision-making and make an impact from day one, this could be the perfect opportunity.
As our Graduate Commercial Strategy Manager, you’ll help support and develop commercial strategies that drive profitable growth, improve performance, and strengthen our position in the market. You’ll act as an important link between the Commercial Director and the wider business - including Sales, Vendor Management, Finance, and Marketing. Your job is to help turn strategic ideas into clear commercial plans, using data and insight to highlight opportunities, spot risks, and drive business-critical decision-making.
You don’t need commercial experience - we’ll teach you that. We do need someone who is:
Ingram Micro is a leading technology company for the global information technology ecosystem. With the ability to reach nearly 90% of the global population, we play a vital role in the worldwide IT sales channel, bringing products and services from technology manufacturers and cloud providers to business-to-business technology experts.
Through Ingram Micro Xvantage™, our AI-powered digital platform, we deliver what we believe to be the industry’s first business-to-consumer-like experience. We also offer a broad range of technology services including financing, specialised marketing, lifecycle management, and technical pre- and post-sales support.
Make an application to join the team! None of this is achievable without great people, with a complete customer focus. Our team is as much about our people as it is our customers and business partners. We want associates with a strong desire to succeed. We offer a competitive base, commission, market leading incentives programme and clear career development. You will receive full training on the products you will be specialising in, and you will have access to a world-leading catalogue of technology-based learning.
If you’re a recent graduate who’s looking for an opportunity to make an impact from day one, work with real data, and be part of a high-performing commercial team, apply now!
